items.title: La Chine ment-elle sur son nombre d’habitants ?
items.description: Dans une étude récente, le démographe Yi Fuxian, auteur du livre Big Country With an Empty Nest , critique de la politique de l’enfant unique et interdit en Chine en 2007, estime que la population réelle du pays en 2020 se situait plutôt aux alentours de 1,27 milliard, et non pas 1,412 milliard comme l’annonçait le recensement officiel China's Population Data Manipulation », Contemporary China Review , Vol. 8, p.2-92, 2026.'> 1 . Cet écart d’environ 140 millions d’habitants, soit à peu près la population de la Russie, pourrait avoir d’importantes implications pour les perspectives du pays, et notamment pour son modèle de croissance. De plus, la Chine a une dette massive dont le service devrait représenter plus de 19 % du budget du gouvernement central cette année, soit 7 points de plus qu’en 2014. Plusieurs faisceaux d’indices suggèrent que les statistiques officielles gonflent artificiellement la population du pays, et ce depuis le début des années 1990. Yi note que le gouvernement a approuvé la distribution d’environ 5,8 millions de flacons par an de vaccin BCG contre la tuberculose, obligatoire pour chaque nouveau-né, entre 2018 et 2020. Or, avec près de 14 millions de naissances par an en moyenne, selon Pékin, entre 9 et 13 millions de flacons auraient été nécessaires : en effet, chaque flacon ne permet en pratique de vacciner qu’environ 1,1 à 1,6 nouveau-né. De même, Yi observe que la taille de la cohorte d’enfants nés en 2000 s’est considérablement réduite quinze ans plus tard, passant de 17,7 millions de naissances selon les statistiques officielles à 14,2 millions de diplômés du collège en 2015, alors même que la scolarité y est obligatoire A Demographic Mirage May Be Distorting China’s Economic Ambitions », The Wall Street Journal , 13 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Plusieurs acteurs auraient pu avoir un intérêt à gonfler les statistiques démographiques : les collectivités locales, afin d’obtenir des financements plus importants de l’administration centrale, le Bureau national des statistiques (BNS) et la Commission du planning familial, afin de légitimer le maintien de la politique de l’enfant unique, mais aussi le pouvoir lui-même, pour qui une correction à la baisse des chiffres de la population aurait pu avoir des conséquences politiques. La correction de décennies de surévaluation de la population pourrait toutefois conduire Pékin à revoir à la baisse ses ambitions géopolitiques. Yi estime en effet que, si l’indice synthétique de fécondité de la Chine se stabilise autour de 0,8 – contre moins de 1 actuellement selon lui –, la population du pays devrait connaître une contraction sans précédent. La Chine passerait de 1,4 milliard d’habitants actuellement, selon les statistiques officielles, à 1 milliard d’ici 2050 puis 620 millions en 2075. En 2100, le pays ne compterait plus que 320 millions de personnes. Elle serait alors moins peuplée que les États-Unis (environ 420 millions d’habitants en 2100, selon les projections des Nations unies) et que l’Europe (environ 470 millions, hors Russie). L’article La Chine ment-elle sur son nombre d’habitants ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Afenyo-Markin reflects on loneliness of public service, says survival is largely spiritual
items.description: Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, the Minority Leader, says friendship, forgiveness and prayer are anchors for survival in politics. He said this on Thursday when the Lorlornyo Haborbor Cultural Group (from Akosua Village in Winneba) paid a surprise courtesy visit to his residence in Accra. Also in attendance were Mr Farouk Mahama, a former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Member of Parliament (MP) for Yendi, and Mr Kwasi Bonzoh, a newly elected Western regional secretary for the NPP. In his address, Mr Afenyo-Markin said he, the former MP and the Western regional secretary, had maintained a close friendship over the years. He referenced a saying attributed to Chinua Achebe, “that visiting a friend to share a meal is not a sign of lack at home but a desire for togetherness,” a value he said should define political engagement. Mr Afenyo-Markin, also the NPP MP for Effutu, recounting the long-standing relationship that had existed between him and the two, said despite occasional disagreements, they had maintained a spirit of forgiveness. Touching on his own political journey, Mr Afenyo-Markin said he did not originally plan to enter public life. He said, “His initial ambition was to practice law, run a business, and eventually become a judge, inspired by jurists like Lord Denning.” He said his entry into politics came at the call of his classmates when a candidate who had won a primary on the ticket of NPP in the Effutu constituency stepped down. “Being in public life is a lonely journey,” he said, describing leadership as “an everyday battle” where one needs trusted people for support. He noted that leadership at any level of the NPP comes with challenges, describing the party as “a party of peers” where disagreements are inevitable. On faith, Mr Afenyo-Markin said prayer remained central to his life. “Ninety-nine per cent of a man’s survival is spiritual. The physical is just one per cent,” he said, adding that adversity comes with public work, and prayer provides resilience.

items.title: Achimota Court designated to handle petroleum diversion cases – NPA CEO
items.description: The Chief Justice, Paul Baffoe-Bonnie, has designated the Achimota Court to handle cases involving the diversion of petroleum products, in a move aimed at strengthening the prosecution of offenders in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector. Chief Executive Officer of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, disclosed this when he appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee. He said the Authority had engaged the Chief Justice to establish a specialised court to deal with offences involving petroleum service providers and facilitate the prosecution of those found culpable. Mr Tamakloe cited the relevant regulations under the National Petroleum Authority Act, Legislative Instrument 2251 (L.I. 2251), which prescribe penalties for the diversion of petroleum products. Under the regulations, anyone convicted of the offence faces a fine ranging from 2,500 to 5,000 penalty units, a prison term of between two and five years, or both. He said the designation of the Achimota Court would provide a dedicated venue for handling such cases and support the enforcement of the regulations.

items.title: Bekwai court jails mine worker 14 years for defiling 8-year-old girl
items.description: The Bekwai Circuit Court has sentenced a 30-year-old mine worker, Atta Kwadwo, to 14 years’ imprisonment for defiling an eight-year-old girl at Manso Kumpese in the Ashanti Region. Kwadwo was convicted of defilement of a child under 16, contrary to Section 101 of the Criminal Code, 1960 (Act 29), as amended by Section 11 of Act 554. The court, presided over by His Honour Isaac Appiatu, found him guilty after hearing the prosecution’s case. According to the prosecution, the incident occurred at about 6 p.m. on July 10, 2026, when Kwadwo accosted the girl near a bathhouse. He reportedly lived in the same compound as the victim’s family. The girl’s mother, concerned that her daughter had spent an unusually long time in the bathroom, went to check on her and found Kwadwo sexually assaulting the child. She raised an alarm, prompting her husband to rush to the scene. Kwadwo was subsequently arrested and handed over to the Adubia Police. A medical examination at St. Martin’s Catholic Hospital in Agroyesum reportedly revealed mild bleeding and lacerations, and a medical form was issued. Although he denied the offence in his caution statement, investigators charged and prosecuted him. The court ultimately found him guilty and sentenced him to 14 years’ imprisonment.

items.title: LdC : l’UEFA désigne le but d’Ezzalzouli face à Porto parmi les plus beaux de la 2e journée
items.description: Le but inscrit par l’international marocain Abdessamad Ezzalzouli lors de la victoire du Real Betis face au FC Porto (3-2), mercredi au stade de La Cartuja, a été retenu par l'UEFA parmi les plus belles réalisations de la 2e journée de la Ligue des champions. Auteur de l’ouverture du score à la 47e minute, l’ailier des Lions de l’Atlas a conclu une belle action collective, initiée par une passe en profondeur de Marc Roca pour Fran García, avant de décocher une frappe enroulée depuis le côté gauche de la surface de réparation, qui a terminé sa course en pleine lucarne, laissant le gardien portugais Diogo Costa sans réaction. Pour le titre de meilleur but de la journée, Ezzalzouli est en lice aux côtés de Samu Aghehowa (FC Porto), Zechiel (Feyenoord) et Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain). Ez Abde with a beauty #UCL pic.twitter.com/pB2s01IwiN — UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) October 15, 2026 Cette rencontre a également mis en lumière la prestation du gardien du Betis, Álvaro Valles, dont l’arrêt décisif à une main en fin de match a permis à son équipe de préserver son avantage et de s’assurer les trois points de la victoire. items.title: Ebola en RDC : plus de 9 000 cas et 4 410 décès, un deuxième cas confirmé au Kenya

items.title: CHASS conference calls for collective action to tackle indiscipline in schools
items.description: Speakers at the 64th Annual National Conference of the Conference of Heads of Assisted Secondary Schools (CHASS) have called for a comprehensive and collective approach to addressing indiscipline in schools, stressing the need for fair rules, responsible leadership, parental involvement and adequate resources. The conference, held in Ho on the theme, “Student Discipline in a Challenging World: Context, Challenges and a Constructive Way Forward,” brought together education officials and school administrators to discuss challenges affecting student behaviour and the delivery of quality education. Mr Haruna Iddrisu, Minister of Education, at the opening ceremony on Wednesday, urged parents, teachers, students, traditional authorities and community leaders to support government’s efforts to tackle indiscipline, describing it as a shared responsibility that extended beyond students to include teachers, public officials and institutions. He said the government was considering regulations to govern conduct in schools and intended to establish a seven-member committee to develop recommendations for addressing the problem. The Minister announced plans to disable social media features on students’ tablets within a week, saying the misuse of mobile phones to facilitate examination malpractice was unacceptable and required collective action. He also outlined measures to improve education infrastructure and teacher welfare, including a proposed GHS750 million teacher housing initiative, the construction of integrated basic schools in every district, and the recruitment of 10,000 additional teachers after the presentation of the 2027 Budget, alongside about 2,000 non-teaching staff. Mr Iddrisu said the government had reviewed the Free Senior High School (Free SHS) programme and identified infrastructure, feeding and quality assurance as major challenges. He cited a 300-million-dollar World Bank-supported initiative, referred to as STAR-J Project, to construct 10 model Category A schools across the country and expand or upgrade more than 100 existing schools. He appealed to CHASS to offer practical recommendations to improve the transparency and merit-based nature of the school placement system. Professor Lydia Aziato, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS) and guest speaker, said efforts to improve student discipline must also examine the conduct of teachers and other school staff. She emphasised that discipline began at home, with parents and guardians playing a critical role in shaping children’s behaviour before they entered secondary school. Prof Aziato urged school heads to ensure fairness in the application of rules and in the general treatment of students. She called for regular student consultation sessions to allow learners to express concerns and understand school decisions, saying open communication could prevent tensions and misconduct. She further advocated stronger mentorship and career guidance, as well as a more flexible education system that recognised alternative pathways to success. She encouraged schools to promote entrepreneurship and practical skills, noting that government employment could not accommodate every graduate. Dr Issahaque Munawaru, Deputy Director-General for Quality and Access at the Ghana Education Service (GES), speaking on behalf of the Director-General, said discipline should focus not only on punishment but also on developing self-control, respect, responsibility and dialogue. He urged school authorities to establish clear and fair rules, apply them consistently, and provide students with opportunities to seek guidance before problems escalated. Dr Munawaru called for stronger partnerships between schools and families, including the reintroduction of Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), subject to the resolution of ongoing legal issues. He said disciplinary measures should protect those affected, hold offenders accountable and help students learn from their actions. He also cautioned school leaders to demonstrate fairness and integrity, saying they could not demand respect from students while tolerating favouritism or undermining their dignity. Reverend Father Stephen Owusu Sekyere, Headmaster of Opoku Ware Senior High School and National President of CHASS, commended government for its support for secondary education, particularly the dedicated funding for Free SHS through the uncapping of the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund), and the restoration of a stable academic calendar. He called for a review of the Student Code of Conduct to equip school authorities to respond effectively to indiscipline in the digital age. Rev Fr Sekyere, however, expressed concern about delays in the release of operational funds and outstanding arrears covering 2021 to 2024. He appealed for a predictable funding mechanism to enable schools to meet their obligations and settle debts. He also urged government to accelerate plans to end the double-track system by 2028, complete stalled GETFund projects and address shortages of classrooms, dormitories, dining halls, furniture, buses and utility vehicles. On digital learning, the CHASS President called for tablets to be provided to all intended students, adequate charging facilities and the blocking of social media platforms on the devices. He also advocated the provision of textbooks so that students would not depend solely on screens for learning. He further urged government to clarify arrangements for the effective operation of PTAs, saying school heads needed to engage parents and seek their support on issues affecting students. The speakers agreed that tackling indiscipline required a balanced approach combining accountability with guidance, fair leadership, family involvement, and a supportive learning environment. They urged school authorities to protect students’ dignity while enforcing school rules and creating conditions that promoted responsible behaviour and effective teaching and learning.
