items.title: Humanitaire : Le Comité International de la Croix-Rouge a 20 ans de présence au Burkina Faso
items.description: Le Comité International de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) célèbre cette année ses 20 ans de présence au pays des Hommes Intègres. L’anniversaire sera marqué par une série d’activité. L’annonce a été faite le vendredi 09 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou autour d’un café presse. Bien avant de parler de cette célébration, l'organisme humanitaire a fait le point de ses activités du premier semestre de 2026. La rencontre a réuni plus d’une quarantaine d'hommes et de femmes de média, au siège de la délégation au quartier Ouaga 2000. Pour ce qui est du bilan du premier semestre, on retient avec Émeline Yameogo/Oboulbiga coordonnatrice communication et prévention du CICR, que les activités menées au premier semestre 2026 ont pu améliorer le quotidien des communautés affectées. On peut estimer que par exemple si je prends en termes de chiffres santé, il y a près de 350 000 personnes qui ont eu accès aux soins de santé qu'il soit curatif ou préventif. Il y a près de 69 000 ménages qui ont reçu une assistance d'urgence à vivre. Il y a aussi près de 20 000 ménages qui ont reçu une assistance pour leur permettre de pouvoir développer leur culture maraîchère >> annonce Émeline Yameogo/Oboulbiga. Pour elle, le CICR a pu contribuer à renforcer l'autonomie et renforcer la résilience des populations. Nous pensons qu'on a pu répondre à notre niveau aux besoins des populations >> se réjouit Émeline Yameogo/Oboulbiga. Février 2006,février 2026, cela fait 20 ans que le CICR est présent de façon permanente au Burkina Faso. Mais il faut savoir que cela fait 30 ans d'engagement, que le Comité international de la Croix-Rouge est aux côtés du Burkina Faso notamment en travaillant avec la Croix-Rouge burkinabè. La commémoration sera assez sobre. Elle sera axée sur la projection d’un CICR qui se veut plus proche, plus efficace et plus pertinent. Il est prévu une campagne digitale pour mettre en lumière les portraits des personnes qui ont marqué les 20 ans de présence du CICR. Un film documentaire sera aussi réalisé pour retracer les faits majeurs de ces 20 ans. Une soirée de commémoration va réunir autour d’une même table différents acteurs, autorités pour faire le point de ces 20 ans. Jean Narcisse KOUDOU L’article Humanitaire : Le Comité International de la Croix-Rouge a 20 ans de présence au Burkina Faso est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: CEB de Kaya II : Les enseignantes sommées de cesser leurs activités commerciales
items.description: À Kaya II, certaines enseignantes auraient troqué, le temps de quelques heures, la craie contre la marchandise. Une concurrence qui ne fait pas rire les commerçantes des écoles et qui a fini par attirer l’attention de l’Inspecteur, désormais décidé à remettre de l’ordre dans les affaires de la classe et celles du marché. À l’école, la vocation première est d’instruire les enfants, pas de leur vider les poches entre deux leçons. Pourtant, dans la Circonscription d’éducation de base (CEB) de Kaya II, certaines enseignantes auraient décidé d’ajouter une corde commerciale à leur arc pédagogique. De quoi transformer, à l’occasion, la salle de classe en annexe de boutique et la récréation en opération de prospection commerciale. Une situation qui n’est manifestement pas du goût des femmes qui tiennent les petits marchés des établissements scolaires. Ces commerçantes, qui comptent sur la vente de leurs produits pour faire vivre leurs familles, se retrouveraient en concurrence avec celles-là mêmes qui sont censées apprendre à leurs enfants les règles de la vie en société. Et comme si la concurrence ne suffisait pas, des élèves seraient contraints d’acheter les marchandises proposées par leurs enseignantes. Pour les commerçantes déjà installées dans les établissements, la pilule serait difficile à avaler. Elles doivent désormais composer avec une concurrence particulière : des vendeuses qui connaissent les élèves, fréquentent les classes et disposent d’une autorité que ne possède pas la vendeuse du petit marché. Face à cette situation, l’Inspecteur, chef de la CEB de Kaya II, a décidé de rappeler que l’école n’est ni une foire commerciale ni un marché parallèle réservé aux détenteurs de craie. Dans une note datée du 12 octobre 2026, il invite les agents concernés à mettre immédiatement fin à leurs activités commerciales dans les établissements scolaires. L’autorité administrative s’appuie notamment sur la loi n° 081-2015/CNT du 24 novembre 2015 portant statut général de la fonction publique d’État, promulguée par le décret n° 2015-1580/PRES-TRANS. L’article 40 de ce texte encadre les conditions dans lesquelles un fonctionnaire peut exercer des activités lucratives. Un rappel qui vaut pour tous les agents de la CEB, qu’ils soient devant un tableau noir ou derrière un bureau. Le message est donc clair : la fonction publique n’est pas un espace où chacun peut improviser son petit commerce au gré des heures de service. L’Inspecteur prévient d’ailleurs que tout manquement aux instructions expose les contrevenants aux sanctions prévues par la loi. De quoi refroidir les ardeurs commerciales de celles et ceux qui auraient pris goût à la vente en milieu scolaire. Fabrice Sandwidi Burkinaonline L’article CEB de Kaya II : Les enseignantes sommées de cesser leurs activités commerciales est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Soirée dansante gâchée à Kona : Pour avoir blessé son jeune parent N.B. risque 12 mois de prison ferme
items.description: Selon des informations rapportées par le quotidien d’État Sidwaya , une soirée dansante dans la commune rurale de Kona a viré au drame judiciaire. Pour avoir asséné des coups au visage du jeune T.G. au cours d'une altercation, N.B. s'est retrouvé à la barre du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Dédougou le mardi 13 octobre 2026. Alors que la victime de 17 ans a subi une incapacité temporaire de travail de 45 jours, le ministère public a requis une peine de 24 mois de prison, dont 12 mois ferme, assortie d'une amende d'un million de francs CFA. Le délibéré de l'affaire a été fixé au mardi 20 octobre 2026. Dans la nuit du 12 au 13 septembre 2026, la commune rurale de Kona, située dans la province du Mouhoun (région du Bankui), accueillait une soirée dansante, relate le journal Sidwaya . Au cours des festivités, un différend a éclaté entre N.B. et T.G.. Souhaitant intervenir dans un conflit opposant T.G. à ses frères, N.B. a appelé ce dernier à l'écart pour lui demander des explications. Malheureusement, l'échange s'est rapidement envenimé pour se transformer en un violent pugilat. Plus âgé et physiquement plus fort que sa victime, N.B. a porté plusieurs coups de poing au visage de T.G.. D'après les détails rapportés par Sidwaya , la violence des coups exercés a entraîné de graves blessures chez T.G., provoquant une incapacité temporaire de travail (ITT) de 45 jours . Pris en charge dans un premier temps au sein de la formation sanitaire locale de Kona, le jeune blessé a dû être transféré vers Dédougou pour bénéficier de soins appropriés. Compte tenu de la minorité de la victime, âgée de 17 ans, son tuteur légal s'est constitué partie civile devant la justice afin d'exiger le remboursement intégral des frais médicaux engagés. Comparaissant devant la barre de l’audience correctionnelle du TGI de Dédougou le mardi 13 octobre 2026, N.B. a reconnu l'intégralité des faits de coups et blessures volontaires qui lui sont imputés, indique le quotidien d'information. Bien que le prévenu ait exprimé ses remords et sollicité la clémence des juges, le Procureur du Faso a souligné le caractère volontaire et caractérisé des violences exercées. Le ministère public a ainsi requis à son encontre une peine de 24 mois de prison dont 12 mois ferme, une amende ferme d'un million de francs CFA ainsi que la contrainte judiciaire fixée au maximum. Le tribunal a mis le dossier en délibéré pour le mardi 20 octobre 2026. items.title: US police identify remains of man found in barrel in shrinking reservoir
items.description: After a years-long investigation, police in Nevada have identified the remains of the person found stuffed in a corroded barrel near Las Vegas. Police identified the man as Edward “Buddy” Lelburian Jackson. He was found in May 2022 with a gunshot wound to the head. The corroded barrel was exposed in Lake Mead after a severe drought caused water levels to drop. His remains went unidentified until recently, when investigators found his family using DNA, according to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department. Robert Price, a homicide detective with the department, said there is no evidence that the death was tied to any known criminal group, despite public speculation that it was mob-related. “At this point in our investigation, we don’t have information to support those theories,” Price said. Jackson is believed to have died after being shot in the head in the 1980s, he said, adding that he was probably in his “mid to late 50s” when he died. He was originally from Arkansas, but was known to travel throughout the US West. He had previously lived in California and Utah, officials say. Authorities have not released new photos of Jackson He was found with a single gunshot wound to the head. The bullet that killed him has not been found, Price said at a news conference on Thursday, adding that nothing else was found in the barrel besides the clothing that he was wearing. He had previously been arrested in Salt Lake City, Utah. Price added that he had no known ties to Las Vegas, and had never been reported missing. Officials displayed a photo of the victim, Edward “Buddy” Lelburian Jackson His extended relatives in Arkansas told police that he was known to move around frequently. “He would travel the country. He would show up when he showed up,” Price explained. Police are still working to identify his killer and any motive in the shooting. Jackson was not known to be a “gambler”, Price said, adding that it could be challenging to track down any of his living associates. The largest US reservoir, Lake Mead, supplies drinking water to 20 million people from Las Vegas to Los Angeles. Police had previously warned that more bodies would probably be found as the lake recedes in drought conditions. Three other people have been found inside and positively identified by authorities. Two are believed to have died from drowning, while a third death remains unexplained. Police had constructed a 3D rendering of the victim’s skull in their effort to identify his remains. Lake Mead levels have been declining since 2000; droughts have been getting worse in recent years, with scientists saying climate change is exacerbating the situation. Droughts have been worsening in recent years, something scientists say is being driven by climate change. Persistent hot summer weather has been causing water levels to drop in rivers and lakes in several countries – leading to unexpected discoveries. In Hungary, the bodies of two World War Two German soldiers were recovered from the Danube River in Budapest earlier this year. Alongside the remains was a largely intact German army Wehrmacht motorcycle. Other remnants of World War Two have recently been found in the Danube, including a broken-up hull near Prahovo in Serbia.

items.title: A chatbot to plug e-governance information gaps
items.description: LAHORE: Getting access to government services can prove costly, time-consuming and confusing. Though a myriad of services are provided through free government-run e-platforms, these remain fragmented across various domains, forcing people to run from pillar to post just to ascertain how they should go about availing a specific service. To solve this problem, a Karachi-based developer has come up with a simple yet elegant solution. The ‘Ask Pakistan’ platform, the brainchild of Raheel Siddiqui, is a website where a chatbot can help people seeking government services obtain the required information, thus bridging the gap between the state and its citizens. Talking to Dawn , Mr Siddiqui said that many non-tech-savvy people struggled with getting the required information. Raheel Siddiqui’s ‘Ask Pakistan’ platform aims to help the less tech-savvy easily access govt services “The information is available and the government is actually good in providing directions on how to avail public services, but the problem is that there are a lot of services. There is no unified platform which can give you information about all of them.” This, he said, was his motivation behind building the platform. The idea came to him when his friend saw a tweet about a US government website that collated all citizen-related services on one page. “He said that it will be great if we have something like this in Pakistan. It took me a couple of hours to build the basic app and I sent it to him. He used it and told me to post about it online, and I did.” Mr Siddiqui didn’t expect a lot of attention and said that he was surprised when it went viral. “I got something like 500,000 views in a few hours,” he added. He described his platform as an information provider and said that it only provided publicly available data, which was already there but was scattered across different government bodies on a large number of separate websites. How it works The pakistangov.online website has a simple interface with bilingual labels for each section, and it greets the user with the message: “Ask anything about a government service. Get a clear answer from official sources, with the next steps.” The website has no sign-up, and it doesn’t require users to input any personal information. According to Mr Siddiqui, privacy was always a concern, which is reflected in how the website is set up. Users can input their queries, with common questions such as “How do I renew my CNIC?” being offered as examples. The questions can be in English, Urdu or Roman Urdu. After processing the query, the chatbot gives a detailed step-by-step answer. The platform currently collates information from 52 government websites, including the Directorate General of Immigration & Passports, National Database & Registration Authority (Nadra), Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Higher Education Commission (HEC), as well as many other federal and provincial departments. For ease of use, users can also browse by topic, and the website also links directly to the most commonly used government departments. Giving an example of availing a government-provided public service, he said that if you want to get a passport, you have to go to the passport office early in the morning, get in line and pay a broker to get a passport. “But if you have a platform where you can get an appointment, after a verification process, you won’t have to go through all this hassle,” he explained, and said that another thing that could happen was that, after filling out the required information through an app at home, the citizen could get their passport without even visiting the office. He said, “This is being done for getting a CNIC and it can also be done for a passport or any other service. Pakistan has the PakID app, which is very good and a lot of services are being offered on it but people don’t know about it.” While internet services are available in villages across the country, there is a lack of awareness about the e-services being provided by the government. “My app focuses on solving this information gap problem. All you have to do is give it a prompt and it can guide you about the required service,” he said. User experience On X (formerly Twitter), many first-time users described their experience of using the ‘Ask Pakistan’ chatbot and praised Mr Siddiqui’s initiative. “Simple and elegant UI makes UX a breeze of fresh air and all the useful links are a cherry on the top,” wrote Muhammad Ishfaque. Another user, Wasey Azim, wrote that he had asked the chatbot a question about Pakistani visas. “It gave an answer no other service could provide,” he said. Usman Shabbir also posted a query about the visa requirements for his US-born son to travel to Pakistan. “I struggled with this question for hours last time I travelled from NYC to Pakistan,” he posted on X, and indicated that he found the answer quite easily thanks to ‘Ask Pakistan’. Many users also called for official integration, with Raja Mannan Khan saying that he was “waiting for agentic AI integration” of the chatbot. Official interest Mr Siddiqui told Dawn that he was surprised when the government showed an interest in his work. Being Gen Z, he said he used to think of the government as a ‘very old-school and laid-back organisation’. “Recently, the IT minister also contacted me and I am talking to the ministry’s team about the future direction of the project. They are very open and I think they have some great ideas and need people to execute these ideas. They have been very good and supportive and asked me what I needed to further this platform,” he said, adding that he was very surprised by it. However, he said that a platform that not only guides but also provides online e-governance services could only be developed and controlled by the government itself. When contacted, Federal Minister for Information Technology (MoIT) Shaza Fatima Khawaja confirmed the ministry’s interest in the project and said that Mr Siddiqui had been invited to the ministry in Islamabad. Subsequently, Mr Siddiqui presented his work to the minister and her team at the MoIT. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

items.title: Banfora : Poursuivi pour avoir imposé trois rapports sexuels à sa copine, un cultivateur relaxé au bénéfice du doute
items.description: La chambre correctionnelle du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Banfora a examiné, le mardi 13 octobre 2026, une affaire de viol qui se serait déroulée dans la nuit du 8 août 2026 à Moussoumourou, dans la province de la Comoé. À l’issue de l’audience, le prévenu a été relaxé au bénéfice du doute, conformément aux réquisitions du ministère public. Appelé à la barre, SS, né le 1er janvier 1984 à Moussoumourou, cultivateur de nationalité burkinabè, père de deux enfants et domicilié dans la localité, a reconnu les faits qui lui sont reprochés, tout en soutenant que les rapports sexuels avaient été consentis. Selon ses déclarations, il a rencontré la victime dans un maquis où elle travaillait comme serveuse. C’est elle qui lui aurait servi une boisson ce jour-là. Il affirme être tombé amoureux d’elle et lui avoir avoué ses sentiments. Après plusieurs jours de réflexion, elle aurait accepté sa proposition. Le prévenu soutient qu’il a ensuite fait part à la jeune femme de son intention d’avoir des rapports sexuels avec elle et qu’elle aurait donné son accord. Ils auraient envisagé de se rendre dans un hôtel à Tiéfora. Cependant, faute de pièce d’identité de la jeune femme, il affirme l’avoir conduite chez un ami. Une fois sur place, une vieille femme leur aurait proposé à manger, ce que la victime aurait refusé. Selon le prévenu, elle lui aurait ensuite conseillé de rejoindre une chambre afin d’éviter les piqûres de moustiques. SS reconnaît avoir eu trois rapports sexuels avec la jeune femme au cours de la nuit, mais affirme qu’elle était consentante. Il explique qu’aux environs de 2 h du matin, elle lui a fait part de son intention de rentrer chez elle. En raison de la menace de pluie, il lui aurait demandé d’attendre. Elle aurait ensuite prétexté vouloir se soulager avant de sortir et de prendre la fuite. Le prévenu affirme s’être également lancé à sa recherche. La victime livre une version différente À la barre, la victime a confirmé avoir connu le prévenu dans le maquis où elle travaillait. Elle affirme qu’il s’était présenté à elle comme un Volontaire pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), en lui montrant une photographie de lui blessé, qu’il aurait présentée comme une preuve de sa participation aux combats. Selon son récit, ayant gagné sa confiance, le prévenu aurait accepté de l’accompagner à l’hôpital parce qu’elle se sentait souffrante. Toutefois, au lieu de la conduire à l’établissement de santé, il l’aurait emmenée chez un ami. La victime explique avoir commencé à s’interroger sur cette destination. Dans la cour, une vieille femme leur aurait proposé à manger, mais elle aurait refusé. Celle-ci lui aurait alors conseillé de rentrer dans une chambre pour éviter les piqûres de moustiques. Elle affirme qu’une fois à l’intérieur, le prévenu l’a rejointe et a fermé la porte. Lorsqu’elle a voulu crier, il l’aurait menacée avant de lui imposer des rapports sexuels à trois reprises au cours de la même nuit. Elle déclare avoir finalement réussi à s’enfuir pendant que le prévenu dormait. Selon elle, ce dernier lui aurait auparavant fait comprendre qu’il comptait la garder enfermée pendant une semaine avant de la libérer. Interrogée par le tribunal sur une éventuelle constitution de partie civile dans l’hypothèse où le prévenu serait déclaré coupable, la victime a indiqué qu’elle ne réclamait rien. Le bénéfice du doute retenu Dans ses réquisitions, le ministère public a demandé la relaxe du prévenu au bénéfice du doute. Le tribunal a suivi ces réquisitions et a prononcé la relaxe conformément à cette demande. Source : Wangola Médias L’article Banfora : Poursuivi pour avoir imposé trois rapports sexuels à sa copine, un cultivateur relaxé au bénéfice du doute est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Burkina/Décolonisation des savoirs : Le professeur Lassina Simporé appelle à repenser l’histoire africaine
items.description: L’enseignant chercheur au département d’histoire et archéologie à l’université Joseph Ki-Zerbo,Pr Lassina Simporé, a appelé jeudi à Ouagadougou une relecture critique des concepts hérités de l’historiographie coloniale, soulignant que la décolonisation des savoirs doit s’appuyer sur la réforme des programmes scolaires, la valorisation des langues africaines et un engagement politique accru. L’Afrique doit repenser son histoire en se libérant des catégories héritées de l’historiographie coloniale, a déclaré le professeur Lassina Simporé, lors d’une communication intitulée « Repenser l’histoire africaine à travers une décolonisation de certains concepts pour construire l’avenir ». Le camarade s’exprimait vendredi 15 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou lors du premier colloque international sur la souveraineté. Pour lui, l’historiographie coloniale a contribué à « marginaliser, dévaloriser et déformer » l’histoire des sociétés africaines. Malgré les indépendances, ces représentations continuent de se retrouver dans les programmes scolaires, les discours et certains comportements sociaux, a-t-il déploré. Il a notamment dénoncé l’usage de la notion de « découverte » pour désigner l’arrivée d’explorateurs européens en Afrique. « Des gens y vivaient déjà, mais on dit qu’il a fallu venir d’ailleurs pour découvrir », a-t-il relevé, appelant à interroger les mots et les concepts utilisés pour raconter l’histoire du continent. Le professeur Simporé a également cité des expressions telles que « peuple sans histoire », « civilisation primitive » ou « mission civilisatrice », ainsi que la réduction de la tradition orale africaine au folklore. Il a estimé que ces formulations participent à une lecture biaisée de l’histoire et entretiennent des complexes chez certains Africains. Selon Lassina Simporé, certains écrits ont refusé d’attribuer aux Africains la construction de structures quadrangulaires découvertes et datées. La communication a également rappelé que plusieurs auteurs enseignants diffusent des théories présentant les populations noires comme inférieures ou dépourvues de contributions significatives à l’humanité. Des écrits notamment à Voltaire et Hegel ont été évoqués pour illustrer la persistance de ces représentations dans les références scolaires et intellectuelles. Pour inverser cette tendance, le professeur a préconisé une reconstruction intellectuelle fondée sur l’examen critique des concepts hérités et la reconnaissance de la diversité des sources historiques. Il a proposé, par exemple, de remplacer l’expression « peuples sans histoire » par celle de « peuples dont l’histoire est transmise par des sources orales ». Au-delà du travail des chercheurs, il a appelé à une action des pouvoirs publics. Celle-ci devrait porter sur la révision des programmes scolaires et universitaires, la refonte des manuels, ainsi que le renforcement de la formation initiale et continue des enseignants. Il a aussi recommandé d’inscrire la décolonisation des savoirs dans les politiques culturelles et mémorielles, de soutenir la recherche menée par les chercheurs africains et de valoriser les langues africaines comme outils de production et de transmission des connaissances. « La déconstruction des concepts hérités de l’historiographie coloniale ne peut reposer uniquement sur les historiens, les chercheurs et les intellectuels », a-t-il conclu, appelant à une mobilisation plus large de la société et des pouvoirs publics. Agence d’information du Burkina LID/ yos L’article Burkina/Décolonisation des savoirs : Le professeur Lassina Simporé appelle à repenser l’histoire africaine est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

Signé en mai dernier, après un an de discussions, cet accord avait mis fin à un bras de fer entre le Niger et ces sociétés chinoises. Cinq mois plus tard, le ministre des Affaires étrangères a rencontré cette semaine les directions de la CNPC, de Wapco et de la Soraz. Lors d'un point de presse, Bakary Yaou Sangaré a dénoncé des manquements de la part de ces sociétés et leur a demandé de se conformer à leurs engagements dans un délai de 45 jours.

items.title: My uncle told me I will never make it in music – Lojay
items.description: Nigerian singer Lojay has revealed that he faced numerous obstacles and doubts, including from family members, when he decided to pursue a career in music. Speaking during a recent livestream with content creator Gilmore, the ‘Monalisa’ hitmaker recalled that one of his wealthy and influential uncles told him he would never succeed in the music industry. “I have an uncle who is now in politics. I won’t mention his name, but he is very rich and popular. When I wanted to start music, he told me I would never blow,” he recalled. Lojay said he did not let doubts discourage him but instead used them as motivation to pursue his ambition. The singer said he was glad that his determination had eventually paid off. He urged his fans to continue believing in their dreams and not allow naysayers to discourage them.

items.title: France : 87 % des électeurs RN excusent les propos présumés "antisémites" de Bardella en raison de son âge
items.description: Les Français sont nettement plus nombreux, 56 % contre 18 %, à croire Mediapart plutôt que Jordan Bardella dans l'affaire des propos antisémites qui lui sont prêtés mais 87% des électeurs RN sont prêts à lui accorder l'excuse de l'âge et seuls 4% d'entre eux pourrait revoir leur vote à l'avenir, selon un sondage publié jeudi. Selon le sondage en ligne, réalisé du 7 au 9 octobre auprès d’un échantillon représentatif de 1.271 personnes par l'institut Cluster 17 pour Marianne, 91 % des personnes interrogées déclarent avoir « entendu parler de l’affaire concernant des messages privés présentés comme antisémites et attribués par Mediapart à Jordan Bardella lorsqu’il avait 17 ans ». Interrogés sur les deux versions qui s’opposent, 56 % des Français accordent davantage de crédibilité à Mediapart. À l’inverse, seuls 18 % considèrent la version de Jordan Bardella comme la plus crédible. Ce jugement est cependant extrêmement dépendant des préférences politiques : 63 % des électeurs RN accordent davantage de crédit à Jordan Bardella. Dans l’hypothèse où les messages seraient authentiques, 50 % des Français considèrent que le fait que Jordan Bardella avait 17 ans à l’époque ne constitue pas une excuse, contre 46 % (87 % des électeurs RN) qui jugent au contraire que cela en est une. Malgré l’ampleur de l’affaire, le socle électoral du RN apparaît très peu déstabilisé : parmi ses électeurs aux européennes de 2024, seulement 4 % répondent que leur vote pour ce parti devient moins probable. Point noir cependant pour le parti d'extrême droite, le sondage met en évidence la persistance d’une image négative sur ces enjeux. Près des deux tiers des Français (64 %) considèrent que le RN véhicule des idées racistes et 57 % estiment qu’il véhicule des idées antisémites. La marge d'erreur est de 1,2 à 2,7 points. The post France : 87 % des électeurs RN excusent les propos présumés "antisémites" de Bardella en raison de son âge appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: What options does Indian law provide for CEC’s removal?
items.description: AMID growing calls for the resignation of India’s top election official Gyanesh Kumar for alleged voter roll manipulation, a key issue has come to the fore: the process of the chief election commissioner’s appointment, resignation and termination. The campaign to remove Gyanesh Kumar from office began after a newspaper report alleged that he was responsible for removing the names of 130 million voters from India’s electoral rolls — a figure slightly higher than Bangladesh’s entire voting population. While the Congress Party, India’s “cockroach” youth movement and others demand Kumar’s resignation, which is simple enough, Kumar’s removal from office is a lengthy and complicated affair, similar to the removal of a Supreme Court judge. Article 324 of the Indian constitution, whi­ch deals with the Election Commission, outlines the procedures for removal of the election chief. Article 324 (5) stipulates that the top election official shall not be removed fr­­om office “except in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court”. In India, the CEC is appointed under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. The CEC is appointed by the president. The law stipulates that people who are serving or have served in positions equivalent to a secretary to the Indian government will be eligible. They also have to be “persons of integrity, who have knowledge of and experience in management and conduct of elections”. A search committee, led by the law minister, compiles a panel of five persons for consideration of the selection committee. The election chief and commissioners are subsequently appointed by the president upon the recommendation of this selection committee, which currently consists of the prime minister, who serves as the chair, along with the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and a minister as nominated by the prime minister. The law governing their appointment, however, witnessed a significant change in 2023 where the constitution of the selection committee was changed. Earlier, the selection panel consisted of the prime minister, opposition leader and chief justice of India. The top judge was replaced by a union cabinet minister, for which Narendra Modi chose his home minister, Amit Shah. Critics argue that this change increases executive influence over the appointment process, as two of the three members of the selection committee would be from the ruling party. As for resigning from office, it is a simple procedure where the election chief or any of the commissioners “may, at any time, by writing under his hand addressed to the president, resign his office”. Removal The election chief’s removal follows a quasi-judicial procedure in line with the procedure stipulated by the Judges Inquiry Act, 1968. Supreme Court and High Court judges can be removed on two grounds — proven misbehaviour and incapacity. A written notice must be signed by at least 100 members of the Lok Sabha or 50 members of the Rajya Sabha. The Lok Sabha Speaker or Rajya Sabha Chair examines the notice and available information, and decides to admit or refuse the motion. If admitted, a committee is convened with one Supreme Court judge, one High Court judge and one distinguished legal expert. The election chief will have the right to defend against the allegation as the committee investigates. If the committee concludes that the charges are not proved, the motion is dropped, and the process ends. If the committee finds that allegations are true, the report is submitted to the parliament. The motion to remove the election chief will have to carry a special majority (two-thirds of voters present and voting) in both houses, in order to pass. If the motion passes both houses, a formal address is presented to the president, who issues the official order of removal. The election chief, Gyanesh Kumar has denied accusations of manipulating the voter list during an exercise to verify India’s one billion voters. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

Martinez apologises for outburst and fined by Man Utd
items.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology following his controversial remarks criticising the club’s hierarchy. After United’s Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, Martinez said the club had left head coach Michael Carrick with an under-equipped squad. Following talks with United on Thursday, the Argentina centre-back released a statement. “Today I met with the club’s leadership and the manager,” Martinez said in a social media post. “It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game. “Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.” It is understood Martinez has been formally punished for his outburst with a fine. Carrick will hold a news conference on Friday, prior to the game against Leeds United on Sunday (14:00 BST). He takes his side to Elland Road on the back of just two wins from nine games this season, placed 13th in the Premier League with six points from as many games. Following the loss to Atletico, Martinez said he expected more investment in the Manchester United squad and “more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]”. The 28-year-old later said he “spoke out of anger and frustration” in making those comments and that he had “belief in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward”. Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane, speaking on The Overlap podcast,, external described the situation at his former club as “a bit of a circus”. Martinez’s statement on Thursday added: “Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that. “I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition: bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve. “With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together.” It remains to be seen whether Carrick selects Martinez for the trip to Leeds . Nevertheless, there is understood to be significant doubt over his long-term future at Old Trafford. His current deal expires at the end of the season but the club have the option of extending it by 12 months. While the issue over his recent comments is now considered closed, the club are still to decide whether they want to trigger the contract option.

items.title: Two killed as rain, snow disrupt life across Gilgit-Baltistan
items.description: • Babusar Pass road closed to all traffic; Diamer police rescue tourists stranded after heavy snowfall • Karakoram Highway remains open despite blockages along route GILGIT: Two young men were killed on Thursday when a landslide struck their vehicle on the Karakoram Highway, as intermittent rain and snowfall disrupted routine life across Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and blocked the Babusar Pass road and other links to remote areas. Local police said Arif Hussain and Kashif Ali, residents of Gul­mat in the Nagar district, were travelling on Karakoram High­way when a rock struck their vehicle in a landslide-prone area near the Pissan section, early on Thursday. Both men were seriously inj­u­red and later succumbed to their injuries. They were shifted to a nearby government hospital, where doctors pronounced them dead. According to the local administration, rain caused landslides at multiple locations in the Nagar section on Wednesday and Thursday. “Heavy rain is currently continuing in the Nagar district, leading to landslides at various locations along the Karakoram Highway. However, the highway remains open to traffic,” a GB police spokesperson said. “The public is advised to contact the Police Helpline at 15 to check the latest status of the highway before travelling.” Meanwhile, authorities said upper areas of GB received intermittent snowfall, while lower areas received rain. “The Babusar Pass road has been temporarily closed to all traffic due to heavy snowfall at Babusar Top,” the police spokesperson said in a statement. “All travellers and tourists are advised to avoid unnecessary travel and to choose alternative routes.” A large number of tourists travelling through the Babusar Pass road toward GB were stranded near the Babusar Top area on Wednesday night. Diamer police personnel rescued the travellers stranded in the snow and brought them safely to Babusar Top, the police spokesperson said. Tourist Police said heavy snowfall received at Khun­jerab Top made the Karakoram Highway potentially dangerous. Traffic between Pakistan and China through the Khunjerab Pass remained disrupted following slippery conditions. Snowfall also continued across the upper areas of the Astore, Skardu, Ghanche, Shigar, Kharmang, Hunza and Nagar districts, creating difficulties for local residents. Many link roads have been blocked. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

items.title: Council of Islamic Ideology worried by law and order situation, Mideast unrest
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Council of Islamic Ideology (CII) met on Thu­rsday and expressed concern over the deteriorating law and order situation in the country, as well as international conflicts involving Middle Eastern countries. In a meeting presided over by CII Chairman Dr Muhammad Raghib Hussain Naeemi, the members discussed terrorism in Pakistan and various legal and national issues, including licences for religious TV networks. During the meeting, the council expressed concern about shipping lines and maritime traffic due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the US-Iran war. The CII members also mentioned the Houthis in a veiled criticism of their intervention in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea. However, the majority decided not to name a brotherly Muslim country in the minutes of the meeting. It may be noted that Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis have been engaged in a fierce conflict for weeks, with the latter closing the crucial waterway. Council supports licences for ‘religious TV channels’; slams attacks on ships using Bab al-Mandeb According to a statement, the council expressed regret over the death of three Pakistanis as a result of attacks by Somali pirates on the high seas and offered prayers for the departed souls. The meeting also approved ringtone messages related to respect for flags and banners used during Muharram. The public service messages to be approved by the telecom regulator would be audible to callers during the month of Muharram, highlighting the sanctity of the month. Licences for channels The council said religious channels should also be issued licences like other channels, not just NOCs, and that laws and rules should be amended accordingly. Currently, there is no category of “religious channels” with the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (Pemra). However, a senior official of Pemra told Dawn that religious channels were not allowed as it could lead to an uneasy situation. Sect-specific channels could provoke sectarianism in the country, the official said, adding that if non-Muslim communities wanted to have their satellite channels under any such policy, this could invite resentment from Muslim clerics. In the wake of the Federal Shariat Court’s decision on the abolition of ‘chaddar and parchi’, the council declared that a special inheritance tribunal should be established to dispose of cases quickly related to women’s property and inheritance. In March 2025, the Federal Shar­iat Court (FSC) said that the cultural and tribal customs of ‘Chaddar’ and ‘Parchi’, which are used to pressure or force women into giving up their ancestral inheritance were un-Islamic and illegal. The council also appreciated the “Muslim Family Laws (Father’s Maintenance) Amendment Bill 2026” presented by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri. The meeting also considered the Shariah status of the application of Article 120 of the Limitations Act 1908 in the matter of recovery of maintenance of children and wives for the past period. The council declared that the rights do not expire even after the time limit for hearing has passed. The CII lauded the Supreme Court’s decision to upho­ld the death sentence of Qaiser Ayub in a blasphemy case, saying that this decision proved that incidents of blasphemy were a reality. The meeting was attended by Allama Tahir Ashrafi and Dr Inti­khab Ahmed Noori, among others. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

items.title: Infantino apologises to FIFA Council – but told he is still not fit to lead
items.description: President Gianni Infantino has apologised to the FIFA Council for his World Cup sell-off plan – but has been told he is not fit to lead unless he releases all the documents and answers key questions. The Fifa Council met in Zurich on Thursday for the first time since Infantino’s secret Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal emerged. Under FFE, which Infantino scrapped within days, a portion of the commercial rights of football’s world governing body would have been given to a private investment firm. In a three-and-a-half-hour meeting, Infantino also faced questions about US striker Folarin Balogun’s suspended red-card ban, the Fifa Peace Prize and funding for national associations. Hours later, Fifa released a video statement from Infantino. He had declined to speak to or take questions from the media, including the BBC. In the FIFA video, he said: “First of all, I apologised for the mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process related to the FIFA Forward Enterprise project, which led to many consequences. “But what is important to remember is that it was a proposal and in no way a done deal, that actually intended to enable Fifa to invest more in our member associations, as opposed to replacing support from existing resources.” Infantino said he would answer questions in writing “in due course”, following what he described as a “constructive discussion” with “different opinions and points of view”. Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt – a Fifa vice-president – said afterwards that many questions remained unanswered despite the “most robust, most frank, most open Council meeting” she had experienced. “One of the disappointing things is that we didn’t get answers to anything that we had specifically requested – for example getting the papers from FFE,” Hewitt said. “I asked the question ‘why not?’ – and we were asked to submit those questions in writing. “I think the man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions now, he’s not fit to be FIFA president – and that was what was shared in the meeting.” Hewitt added: “I’ve repeatedly asked for the papers to be shared. I haven’t received them, and even after today’s request, I still haven’t received them. “It is the rationale for why FFE happened in the way that it did, the Balogun case, the Peace Prize. “The responses to those questions, which I still don’t have answers to, will determine, from my personal point of view, whether or not Gianni is the right candidate. “That will be the point at which or not we can say that any individual that was involved in FFE can or cannot be trusted because until we see what actually happened it’s very difficult to say behaviour needs or not to change.” Hewitt acknowledged there had been “some contrition” in Infantino’s apology. “Then there were no holds barred in terms of what we felt about what had happened,” she added. “What he really apologised for was not bringing it to the Council. If you regret it that deeply, share it with us.” UEFA – European football’s governing body – has been one of Infantino’s fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down. It has initiated criminal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts to obtain all documents related to FFE . Hewitt hopes Infantino now freely releases the documents so the Council can understand what happened. “Those papers coming to Council are a crucial next part of us feeling comfortable as to what, if any, criminal proceedings need to take place,” Hewitt said. Asked if there was any change in stance from UEFA about Infantino, she added: “From my position, nothing has shifted. I’ve no new information that makes me feel any differently, other than we do have a president who is apologetic.” UEFA still searching for candidate to stand against Infantino Infantino will stand for re-election as Fifa president for a third time in March, and as yet no credible candidate has emerged to challenge the Swiss-Italian. Former Tottenham and Switzerland defender Ramon Vega has said he intends to run, but it appears unlikely he will get the five letters of support from member associations let alone be a serious contender. Senior figures within European football have told BBC Sport they want former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to run. But it is unclear whether Wenger would be prepared to give up his position as Fifa’s global head of football development for a fight against his boss that he may not win. Hewitt said UEFA – and Infantino’s other opponents around the world – must find someone to put their name on the ballot before the deadline of 18 November. She also indicated it would be important for the president to have a rival after being re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023. “I think it’s important to Gianni to have somebody who stands with a different manifesto, and good for Fifa to have that choice,” Hewitt added. “We’re in a democracy here. We must remember there are 211 associations and it’s really important that all 211 associations have the opportunity to vote according to how they feel. “This is somebody who puts football first and foremost right at the heart of everything that they do. Secondly, it has to be somebody who unites the world. Thirdly, somebody who needs to have the courage to bring about reforms.” Hewitt said Balogun avoiding a suspension after being sent off at the World Cup was one of the “biggest issues”. Balogun’s ban was suspended after US President Donald Trump asked for the decision to be reviewed. BBC Sport understands a proposal was put to the Council to amend the Fifa disciplinary code, which would prevent a repeat. Under that, regulations would be amended to state the disciplinary committee could not suspend an automatic one-match ban for a red card. Fifa’s legal committee will review and update Fifa Council in December. “What happened in July did not serve football… whether it’s the Balogun case, the FFE case… the reputation of football was put under serious threat,” said Hewitt. “Once behaviour starts to influence what happens on the pitch, then I think it’s a dark day for football and a number of people said that in the room.” The Fifa Peace Prize – awarded to President Trump – was also raised, but Hewitt said Infantino’s behaviour with “other maybe celebrities and dignitaries” was also discussed. “When he puts other dignitaries in front of his 211 associations, then he’s lost what football is about,” Hewitt said. “And that was said by a number of people, not just the Europeans.” How the Peace Prize came to be awarded will be the subject of an investigation by the Fifa social committee which will report back in December. “They will consider, first of all, how the Peace Prize came about, whether it should have come about, whether it should have been awarded in the way that it was, who made that decision and whether or not it should be taken out or whether it should be reformed,” Hewitt said. “That committee will report back to Council in December and then Council will make the decision based on its recommendation. “Today there was a watershed moment where it’s very clear in order to move forward, which we all want to do, we have to understand the past.”

items.title: Trump banking on ‘swift end’ of Iran war to bring down fuel prices
items.description: • Pezeshkian decries US blockade, insists ‘military force’ will not compel Tehran into submission • Washington weighs using ‘Mother Of All Bombs’ against Iranian energy sites, CNN reports WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump once again predicted a swift end to the war with Iran, and a sharp drop in oil prices once the conflict concludes, even as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian warned that military action cannot force them into submission. “The Iran war will end very soon … Soon, as they want it to end,” Trump told reporters in Montana. “They’ll never have a nuclear weapon, and oil prices will drop like a rock.” According to Anadolu Agency , Trump also expressed uncertainty over which Ira­nian officials the US was negotiating with. “They don’t have a navy. They don’t have an air force. Their army is decimated. Their leaders are gone,” Trump said. “I should have probably left their leaders because I don’t know who the hell we’re negotiating with.” “Iran was the bully of the Middle East,” he said, adding that the country was no longer as powerful as it had been. Trump also claimed that US strikes had destroyed Iran’s naval fleet and rendered its military aircraft unusable. He said Iran had 159 ships and asserted that none remained operational, while also claiming that its fighter jets had been destroyed on the country’s runways. ‘Iran won’t submit to force’ Meanwhile in Tehran, President Pezeshkian warned that military action cannot force a country into submission, adding that his country “must find a way to strengthen national cohesion and unity”, Al Jazeera reported. He said that the country was facing its most intense blockade since the 1979 Revolution, accusing the United States of seeking to provoke public protests. “Over the 48 years since the Revolution, we have never faced such intense blockade, war and difficulties as we are facing now,” Pezeshkian said in a speech broadcast by state television. He accused Washington of seeking to make life difficult for Iranians to fuel public anger and trigger unrest. Pezeshkian said the US was focusing its efforts on making “the people become upset and face difficulties, and then for social protests to emerge so that they can achieve their sinister objectives”. ‘Mother Of All Bombs’ Meanwhile, the US is considering using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB) bomb — better known by its nickname, the “Mother Of All Bombs” — against Iran if Trump decides to renew combat in the deadlocked war, CNN reported on Thursday. The military is planning for the potential use of the weapon to target Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, according to the news outlet, which quoted officials familiar with the matter. “The MOAB is a massive information operation type weapon that is great for huge area clearance but not much else,” a source familiar with the plans told CNN. “It is definitely not designed as a deep penetration warhead.” Trump is trying to boost his low approval ratings ahead of November’s midterm elections , with polls showing the unpopular war in Iran and the fuel and other price rises it has caused are hurting his Republican Party. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been at an impasse since the summer, and Washington has in recent weeks dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure. However, officials have raised doubts over the efficacy of the bomb if deployed, particularly its ability to destroy suspected underground nuclear sites in Iran, as well as concerns over possible civilian casualties from such a huge weapon. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

items.title: Southgate does not see return to Premier League management
items.description: Former England manager Gareth Southgate says he does not see himself returning to club management in the Premier League. The 56-year-old has been out of management since resigning as Three Lions boss after guiding them to the Euro 2024 final, where they lost to Spain. Southgate, who also took England to the Euro 2020 final, has not managed at club level since a three-year spell with Middlesbrough from 2006. When asked whether he would consider returning to managing in the Premier League, he told The Amol Rajan Connection podcast, “I don’t see a scenario where I do that.” He added: “Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying it; at the very least, for a period, the wins keep you going. “By the end, I didn’t even enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes. So, I’ve hardly watched football. “I went to the FA Cup final to see my team, Crystal Palace , win their first trophy. I’ve not been to a football ground since. So my sort of desire to be involved in football has changed.” Since leaving the England role, Southgate has also spent time working in the media, and earlier this year he fronted a BBC documentary where he travelled across the UK to understand challenges facing young men and boys. He has also spent time as a visiting lecturer at Harvard Business School in Boston. “I’ve loved the last 18 months of my life,” he added. “I’ve had 37 years where my sense of self depended on whether I won or lost on Saturday. And actually I’ve loved having different experiences. I’ve met politicians, I’ve met people in the media industry, I have learned about leadership in all sorts of areas, I’ve travelled around the world learning things. “I’ve just enjoyed playing a different film in my life.” ‘No winners’ in Manchester City charges Last month, Manchester City were found guilty of the majority of charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. An independent commission found that, during that time period, the club arranged “sham contracts” as well as “relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs”. The club have denied any wrongdoing and submitted an appeal on 2 October. “There’ll be the tribal fans’ response to punish Manchester City as much as we can, relegate them, fine them, do whatever you can,” added Southgate. “I’ve been in football boardrooms, I’ve been in meetings with Uefa, I’ve been in meetings with Fifa, I have been in all these spaces and I know how complicated all of this is. “My underlying thought is none of this is good for football and there are no winners because if you’re at the Premier League, for a very brief moment you might feel justified that all the flak you’ve had for this case taking so long, this is why it’s taken so long and there’s the verdict, and I’m sure there’s an element of justification in that. “Then there’s this realisation of how do we deal with all of this because you know the possibility of all the different legal cases that emerge from this, how long this could still take, what’s the right sort of punishment, how do you keep the whole game on track? “That’s unbelievably complex.”

items.title: Could Wenger really take on Infantino and run for the FIFA presidency?
items.description: Despite the backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors, Fifa president Gianni Infantino looks increasingly likely to be re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term next year. But could there be a sensational twist? Senior figures within European football have told BBC Sport they want former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to run as a surprise candidate. But would the man who has been the governing body’s head of global development since 2019 really challenge his own boss? And what lies behind the support he has? On Thursday, the FIFA Council will meet for the first time since the emergence of Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme plunged the organisation into crisis, leading to calls from the game’s leaders in Europe, North America and Asia for him to step down. A defiant Infantino will come face to face with some of his fiercest critics at what could be a spicy gathering in Zurich. Fifa is set to propose a $3.4bn (£2.6bn) increase in the amount of money it hands out for football development. But Infantino will also face scrutiny over governance reforms, FFE, the awarding of the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize last year to US President Donald Trump, and disciplinary procedures in the wake of the Folarin Balogun affair. But the meeting will also bring into sharp focus the failure so far to identify a unifying figure with the worldwide appeal to challenge Infantino. While potential rivals like Victor Montagliani, the president of the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (Concacaf), and Uefa chief Aleksander Ceferin have let it be known they are not contenders, Infantino has been busy touring the world, shoring up his position. The growing expectation is that such is the support he retains in his power base of Africa, South America and Oceania, he will be returned, despite only carrying the backing of roughly half of Fifa’s 211 members. To date, the only person to declare their intention to run is the former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega, although few rate his chances. So could Wenger be the answer? Here in Zurich, there is no indication that he is plotting a bid. On Wednesday evening Wenger joined Infantino and other Fifa Council members for dinner in a Zurich restaurant. As a senior member of Fifa’s management team, he will also be present at Thursday’s meeting. When BBC Sport asked about his intentions via Fifa, no comment was provided. Meanwhile, those close to the 76 year-old, who left Arsenal in 2018 after 22 years in which he became the most successful manager in the club’s history, will not be drawn on whether he is interested. One told BBC Sport he would be “an ideal candidate, but he is his own man”. What is clear is that he does have supporters, who believe he commands the level of respect beyond Europe that would be essential if the Uefa-led rebellion against Infantino is to have any chance of success. “He isn’t a football politician, but it would bring football and integrity to the leadership of Fifa” says Alex Phillips, a former Uefa and Fifa executive told the BBC. “It’s become way too much focused on money and not enough focused on football. And I think someone like that would put football back as the main priority. Let’s see what he decides. There may be other candidates as well.” A current senior official at a European national association agrees that Wenger “truly understands football development because he’s been running it. “People don’t see him as just a European. He’s very respected in Asia, for instance, from his time working in Japan. A lot of people are saying he’d be the ideal candidate. With him, it’s not about money, status or ego. He genuinely loves the game. “He’s made a difficult role work and understands Fifa, and that’s why he’d be a really good candidate. “That said, he’s in a really difficult position.” That was highlighted amid the fallout over FFE, when Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot. “I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports,” Wenger said in a statement at the time. “The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity.” Some may have expected Wenger to resign over the controversy, given his thinly veiled criticism of Infantino, the way he had been kept in the dark, and the condemnation of the plot from stakeholders across the game. But he has carried on in a role in which he oversees youth development at academies in 60 countries, as well as youth competitions around the world. He is also a technical adviser to rule-making body International Football Association Board (Ifab). Wenger has caused controversy at times in his Fifa role, notably for proposals such as biennial World Cups , and the idea of a ‘daylight’ offside law. But he also has a global profile, including in Africa, where Infantino recently received a major re-election boost when receiving the backing of all 54 member national associations after promising an increase in funding. Known as a champion of African players when in charge at Arsenal, Wenger’s support of an expanded 48-team World Cup in order to drive development in countries beyond the game’s traditional powers has been well received in the continent. Indeed, at the weekend Wenger was in Cape Verde at a Confederation of African Football conference, telling the delegates: “We want to see an African team win the World Cup, and the numbers show that it is feasible.” Such sentiments would do him no harm if he was to stand for president. BBC Sport has been told that a large number of Fifa’s staff also want Wenger to run, and believe he could change the organisation’s image. Others, however, are more sceptical. One well-connected figure in Fifa circles told BBC Sport that he would be “amazed if Wenger would rise up against the man who appointed him in the first place. Arsene has had some fairly ‘out there’ ideas. In terms of the administration of the game and the relationships on a political level, in the kind of places you’re going to need to corral and command power, I’m not sure he’s the man for that.” Another senior European official said: “He has the stature, but I’m not sure he smacks of the future. Maybe he could do a single term to introduce reforms. He is very respected in the game and has done a good job of the development programmes, but whether he’d split from Gianni, I just don’t know.” If Wenger does want to run, he has until 18 November to declare his candidacy, and would need to be nominated by at least five national associations. As a manager, Wenger is remembered as a legendary figure who changed English football with his forward-thinking approach to tactics and nutrition. Could he attempt a shake-up of a different kind at Fifa? It is an intriguing prospect.

items.title: AJK assembly speaker calls for consensus on future of refugee seats
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq has called for a broad-based consensus on the future of refugee seats in the assembly, urging political leaders to help resolve the current crisis through dialogue and reforms. Speaking to journalists at the Speaker House on Thursday, Mr Fa­­rooq said political leaders had an opportunity to align themselves with national objectives and provide guidance by finding a way forward rather than dwelling on the past. “Learning from mistakes is wisdom. We need to explore new avenues for the future,” he said, adding that he supported reforms in all institutions. AJK could not progress with its large administrative structure and high expenditure, he said, while maintaining that the newly elected government, comprising young people, should be given an opportunity to move in the right direction. Backs institutional reforms, says electricity and flour subsidies will continue He also said subsidies on electricity and flour would not be withdrawn, though relief and concessions should be targeted on the basis of data. Distinguishing between constitutional offices and the executive, he claimed that although power was influential, the assembly speaker was not part of the government, just as the state president was not. “The assembly is not the government; the cabinet and the prime minister constitute the government,” he said. The government had been in office for only a few weeks, and the second phase of cabinet formation was still pending. It would be completed upon the return of PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif to Pakistan, he said. Mr Farooq said the government and cabinet had not been expanded because elections in seven constituencies of Poonch division were still pending. Without representation from these areas, he added, the government could not be considered complete and fully functional. Poonch situation Mr Farooq said informal negotiations were under way through the AJK president to improve law and order and ease tensions in Poonch. He expressed the hope that backchannel contacts would produce positive results and urged the media to avoid speculation until the talks yielded an outcome. He accused the PPP of attempting to exploit the Poonch situation for political gain during its brief stint in power, adding that the phased elections had been held with the party’s consent. The speaker said the state president and the entire political leadership should come forward to find solutions through dialogue. Political parties and their leaders had a responsibility to play an effective role, he said, adding that the process of rendering them irrelevant and ineffective had begun during the previous assembly. Mr Farooq recalled that he and some other PML-N leaders had called for a fact-finding commission a year ago to examine the circumstances contributing to the current situation, but no political party had supported the proposal. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

items.title: Nigeria’s inflation rate eases slightly but still a worry for many citizens
items.description: Nigeria’s headline inflation rate slowed slightly last month, data showed on Thursday, but it remains stuck around 15% in annual terms and is a concern for many citizens months before a national election. Consumer inflation was 14.63% year-on-year in September, down from 15.39% in August, the National Bureau of Statistics said. Food inflation was largely unchanged at 19.59% in September, up from 19.57% in August. Stubborn price pressures are a ​test for President Bola Tinubu ahead of January’s election, when he ​will seek a final four-year term. “The common man is suffering. Everything has skyrocketed,” Michael Udoariri, a 44-year-old who works in an insurance company and is ​a father of three, told Reuters at a bus stop ​in Lagos while waiting to go to work. He said soaring fuel costs had ‌forced ⁠him to stop driving and switch to public transport. The central bank surprised investors last month with a 350-basis-point interest rate cut to 23%, saying that market rates had diverged from its benchmark rate and that previous tightening measures had proven effective. Tinubu took office in 2023 and implemented a series of economic reforms, such as cutting petrol subsidies and devaluing the currency, to boost ​economic growth and bolster public finances. But those reforms also spurred a cost-of-living crisis. Economic growth has picked up , coming in at about 4.4% year-on-year in the ⁠second ​quarter, but it remains well below ​the 7% annual rate Tinubu has targeted by 2027.

items.title: PTA shares tips to improve calls, internet quality
items.description: • Urges users to turn on 4G/LTE, VoLTE settings on their phones • Consumers with older SIM cards told to upgrade for 4G support ISLAMABAD: The Pak­i­stan Telecommu­nica­tion Authority (PTA) adv­ised mobile phone users on Thursday to adjust their network settings and adopt newer technologies, including Voice over Long-Term Evolution (VoLTE), Wi-Fi Calling, and VoWiFi, to improve their calling and mobile internet experience. Responding to consumer complaints regarding unclear voice quality and connection delays on 4G and LTE calls, the telecom regulator recommended that users verify their handset network settings and activate the 4G/LTE option if it is not already switched on. The authority urged consumers to enable VoLTE, Wi-Fi Calling and VoWiFi options on their phones, noting that the availability and use of these facilities depend on compatibility between the handset and the relevant mobile operator. The guidance is primarily relevant to regions where 4G service is expanding following a recent spectrum auction. According to the regulator, VoLTE enables voice calls over a 4G network, which improves voice quality and speeds up call connections. To benefit from the facility, however, the handset, the SIM card and the mobile operator must all support the technology. For areas where mobile signals are weak, such as inside homes or in basements, the authority said Wi-Fi Calling and VoWiFi could be particularly useful. VoWiFi technology makes Wi-Fi Calling work, allowing users to place calls over a Wi-Fi connection provided their handset and operator support the feature. Users must enable the Wi-Fi Calling option in their phone settings and connect to a Wi-Fi network. Consumers must also ensure that both their phone and SIM support 4G services. Because many older SIM cards do not support 4G or VoLTE, the regulator suggested that users upgrade their SIMs. The 4G/LTE standard is the fourth-generation mobile network technology which offers faster mobile internet speeds than 3G. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

items.title: Ghana ranked joint 6th in 2026 Absa Africa Financial Markets Index
items.description: Ghana has been ranked joint 6 th with Botswana in the 2026 Absa Africa Financial Markets Index (AFMI). The nation scored 64, up from 58 recorded in 2025. The improvement in the rankings was as a result of big gains in equities and companies listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange. South Africa maintained its 1 st position with a score of 85, up from 83 in 2025. Its improvement was attributed to inflation-targeting reset and price-marking reforms Mauritius (77), Namibia (71), Uganda (68) and Kenya (65) placed 2 nd , 3 rd , 4 th and 5 th respectively. The report stated that the macroeconomic environment improved across much of the region. All 29 AFMI countries recorded stronger gross domestic product growth scores, providing a more supportive backdrop for investment and capital markets activity. Inflation declined in 20 countries and external debt as a share of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) also improved in 20 economies. These gains strengthened confidence and supported increases in market size, depth and liquidity across most AFMI countries. Zambia benefitted from an increase in its outstanding sovereign bonds, while Ghana’s turnover in the fixed income market and corporate trading rose. However, some vulnerabilities remain. Zimbabwe, Malawi and Ethiopia remain in debt distress, while liquidity remains a central constraint. Over the last 10 years, the Absa Africa Financial Markets Index has assessed financial development in African countries based on measures of market accessibility, openness and transparency. It tracked progress across 29 African countries through a survey of more than 50 organisations based in the region. Supported by the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, the index is a benchmark for examining how progress enhances investment appeal and promotes economic resilience. The 2026 report further examined developments in Africa’s financial landscape, including the diversification of financial products, the adoption of environmental, social and governance frameworks, the future of digital innovation and efforts to strengthen regulatory frameworks.

items.title: Judicial commission on Mir Raza’s murder hands over sealed report to Sindh govt
items.description: KARACHI: A sealed report prepared by the judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in Mir Raza Ali’s murder investigation was handed over to the provincial government on Thursday. The commission, headed by Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court, concluded its proceedings last week after examining 49 witnesses during 15 hearings, including inspection of the crime scene. The inquiry report along with associated documents was handed over to focal person of the provincial government and additional secretary of home department Javed Ahmed Abro by registrar of the commission Abdul Majid on the premises of the SHC. As Justice Sial was hearing cases at the SHC Hyderabad circuit court, the registrar of the commission handed over the sealed report along with the entire record of the proceedings to the provincial authorities. It’s up to provincial authorities whether to make the document public or keep it secret, says official According to a communication sent by registrar Abdul Majid to the chief minister of Sindh through the focal person, since Justice Sial has been sitting at SHC Hyderabad pursuant to the roster commencing from Oct 12, the registrar has handed over the sealed report to the focal person along with executive summary, statements of witnesses and other supplementary documents. After receiving the record, Mr Abro told reporters that he would hand over the sealed report along with other record to the provincial government and it was the prerogative of the government to decide whether the inquiry report was to be brought into the public domain or otherwise. In August the provincial government formed the commission, which was tasked with making recommendations for further investigation and forensic analysis or legal/departmental action and it was required to submit its findings and recommendations to the Sindh government within 30 days. However, the commission had struggled to meet its deadline and sent an application last month to the Sindh government for an extension in its tenure till Oct 15. Therefore, the provincial cabinet granted an extension. Besides examining 49 witnesses and available record, the commission had also sent questionnaires to Karachi police chief Azad Khan, head of current investigation team DIG Amir Farooqui and DIG East Farrukh Lanjar after dismissing an application of aggrieved family to summon the senior police officers to testify before the commission. Therefore, the three police officers had submitted written answers before the commission through a commissioner appointed by the commission. The 25-year-old businessman and Institute of Business Administration graduate, Mir Raza Ali, had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS and his body with gunshot wounds was found a day later in bushes in a Gulistan-i-Jauhar’s locality. Initially, the police built the case around suicide on the basis of the first autopsy, which indicated a bullet entry wound on the chest, and by pointing out business losses and money borrowed by the victim. However, police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had disputed the findings of the first post-mortem conducted by medico-legal officer Dr Osama Sheikh. Published in Dawn, October 16th, 2026

items.title: Wang Yi urges Israel to open Gaza routes, halt West Bank settlements
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Thursday called for the full opening of access routes into Gaza to prevent a worsening humanitarian disaster and urged Israel to halt and reverse settlement activities in the West Bank. Wang, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during a meeting with Israeli President Isaac Herzog in Baku on the sidelines of the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA). China and Israel have maintained stable relations and achieved positive results in practical cooperation over the past three decades, Wang said. He expressed China's willingness to use the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year as an opportunity to deepen cooperation and strengthen public support for bilateral ties. He stressed that the Palestinian question is the greatest historical injustice of the 21st century and that the two-state solution is the right path to resolving it. China stands ready to work with the international community to bring all parties back to dialogue and negotiations and seek a political solution to the conflict, Wang said, adding that both Palestinians and Israelis have the right to live in peace and to establish independent states. Herzog said Israel firmly adheres to the one-China policy and hopes to advance friendly ties with China, including cooperation in science and technology, investment and people-to-people exchanges. He said Israel hopes for peace but faces threats and challenges to its national security that require a strong response. Herzog also praised China's efforts to promote regional peace and stability, saying Israel values China's proposals and initiatives and is willing to maintain communication with Beijing.

items.title: EU summit focuses on competitiveness, energy prices
items.description: European Union (EU) leaders gathered in Brussels on Thursday for a two-day summit which focused on economic competitiveness, high energy prices and the bloc's next long-term budget, with the first day ending amid differences in views and the cancellation of a scheduled press conference. According to the European Council's agenda, economic challenges take center stage, with EU leaders expected to provide guidance to the European Commission on targeted, temporary short-term measures to ease the impact of high energy prices on businesses and households. They will also discuss longer-term efforts to reduce Europe's dependence on fossil fuels. A recent surge in energy prices has heightened concerns over the EU's competitiveness. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen recently told the European Parliament that natural gas prices in Europe had risen by 140% since late February, while diesel prices had doubled, adding around 100 billion euros (about $112.1 billion) to the bloc's fossil fuel import bill. With winter approaching, high energy costs could place further strain on European industries and households. The EU's next long-term budget is another major item on the agenda. Leaders will continue discussions on the Multiannual Financial Framework for 2028-2034, seeking to consolidate key elements needed to reach a final agreement by the end of 2026. The summit will also address continued support for Ukraine, including its critical infrastructure needs ahead of winter, as well as European security and defense, migration, EU enlargement and the situation in the Middle East.
