items.title: A Bold Era in Hollywood Ends With a Whimper
items.description: Sign up for Video Village , a new weekly newsletter in which David Sims unearths cinematic gems and brings readers into his movie obsession. To kick off this newsletter, I sent out a message declaring that movies were “ undeniably back .” Within days, it seemed that the sky was falling again. Two venerable studios, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, officially merged on October 6, further consolidating power in Hollywood into just a few conglomerates. The new entity has been dubbed Skydance, the name of the original production company that CEO David Ellison founded in 2006. Not much has outwardly changed thus far, new moniker aside. But internally, Ellison has already made at least one concerning decision. Once the deal closed, two key leaders at Warner Bros., the bolder and more risk-taking of the two studios, were immediately shown the door: Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy, the co-chairs of Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group. Their departure suggested what many industry analysts had feared: that their new boss was no longer a fan of taking big, bold risks. After all, the news that De Luca and Abdy were exiting the company —to be replaced by Paramount’s current team, which will oversee what has been referred to as the “Paramount Warner Bros. Motion Picture unit” (try saying that three times fast)—arrived right before a historically bad weekend for the studio. The Tom Cruise project Digger opened on October 2 to only $8 million domestically, on a budget that reportedly climbed as high as $180 million; that’s an especially anemic number given Cruise’s involvement as both star and co-producer. Digger now stands as Warner Bros.’ final release before it joined Skydance, and the movie’s catastrophic box-office performance is the latest in a series of tough beats for the company this year. Given the film’s wild ambition, its failure will also be a fitting coda for an era that was very up-and-down financially—but often creatively thrilling. De Luca and Abdy took over Warner Bros. Pictures in 2022, bringing with them a strategic reset. They were both well-regarded names in the world of awards-friendly indie cinema, shaking up a studio that was bouncing back from a theatrical strategy unpopular with the industry: putting blockbusters on HBO Max the day they were released. De Luca was a storied executive whose career included green-lighting boundary-pushing projects by Paul Thomas Anderson and David Fincher and earning Best Picture Oscar nominations for such movies as The Social Network and Moneyball . Abdy started out her career at Danny Devito’s hyper-cool Jersey Films and worked on The Revenant and The Big Short , among other awards-season hits, as president of the production outfit New Regency. Together, they presided over a splashy period at Warner Bros. in which they focused on recruiting big stars and major auteurs while they also shed the remains of the prior leadership’s flailing, expensive approach to the DC Comics franchise. But their results were inconsistent: In 2023, the giant success of Barbie in the summer and Wonka at Christmastime buoyed the studio. The following year, Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga and Joker: Folie à Deux were such expensive flops that industry experts began predicting De Luca and Abdy would soon lose their jobs. Instead, last year, the duo spearheaded a cinematic slate that will likely be spoken about in hushed tones in Hollywood C-suites for generations. A Minecraft Movie took advantage of its kid-friendly IP to make nearly $1 billion worldwide, despite being barely coherent. The relaunch of the DC cinematic universe went splendidly with Superman , directed by the new DC Studios co-chair, James Gunn. The silly sequels Final Destination Bloodlines and The Conjuring: Last Rites punched above their weight commercially. Zach Cregger’s Weapons was not just a horror hit but also a critical favorite that won major awards. Ryan Coogler’s Sinners , whose high budget met prerelease skepticism from box-office analysts, was a cultural sensation and a financial boon. And Anderson’s blockbuster, One Battle After Another , earned just enough money to justify its scale before taking the Oscar for Best Picture. In basically each of these cases, De Luca and Abdy’s calculation of betting on creators who had an established track record and pairing them with reliable stars worked. Meanwhile, safe comic-book and video-game adaptations helped shore up any business concerns. This year, however, the same approach has resulted in a lot of swings and misses. Collaborations between acclaimed directors and performers, such as Maggie Gyllenhaal and Jessie Buckley’s The Bride! , failed to make back their budget; Supergirl and Practical Magic 2 were box-office disappointments, in part because of poor reviews. Warner Bros. couldn’t even claim the surprise success of Coyote vs. Acme , a Looney Tunes movie that it sold to the indie distributor Ketchup Entertainment after deciding in 2023 not to release it ; it became a sleeper family hit this summer. Maybe Digger flopping was the final straw for Ellison. Or maybe the Skydance CEO was always intent on keeping his own team in charge. Paramount has adopted a more populist, risk-averse strategy since Ellison took over that studio in 2025. This year’s schedule included crowd-pleasing horror films and a Jackass clip-show-style sequel, although none was particularly successful with theatergoers; a new live-action Street Fighter and the latest edition in the Angry Birds franchise are on the way. Indeed, it even has a Tom Cruise movie on the slate for 2028—but rather than being an auteurist effort like Digger , it’s a sequel to the 1990 NASCAR drama Days of Thunder that I’d argue nobody was really asking for. Skydance seems to be planning to keep Paramount and Warner Bros. separate, the industry reporter Matthew Belloni suggested in a Puck column last week. Ellison has also promised that Skydance will keep up a furious pace of releases, perhaps in recognition of Hollywood’s agita when Netflix almost got its hands on Warner Bros. during the merger drama; the concern was that films released as part of “Netflix Warner Bros.” would not be shown in cinemas at all. But the departure of De Luca and Abdy certainly suggests that any weirder Hail Mary passes will be few and far between. Sure, they haven’t all worked—but a hit like Sinners doesn’t happen without a couple of other tough throws that fail to connect. Meanwhile, some viewers are seemingly already reclaiming Digger as a cult classic; maybe that’s just quick-turn nostalgia for a moment in Hollywood that appears to be further slipping away. Or perhaps it’s a sign that some portion of the audience will always be clamoring for audacious work—the kind that is and will still be made by studios of all sizes. Just maybe not by Warner Bros., going forward. An Essay I Enjoyed Illustration by Paul Spella* The Most Cursed Team in American Sports By Kaitlyn Tiffany The mythical story of the Buffalo Bills could be told like this: Their fans are crazy and live in the snow. They shovel this snow out of their stadium to help their godforsaken football team, which, until recently, was most famous for losing the Super Bowl four times in a row in the early 1990s. According to one theory, those failures fed into Timothy McVeigh’s derangement before he planned and executed the Oklahoma City bombing. The franchise was an utter disaster, for the most part, until the 2018 arrival of an otherworldly quarterback named Josh Allen, who has exhibited many heroics. But he has yet to bring his team to the Super Bowl. Read the full article. Coming Attractions A gorgeous new release this week is William and David Greaves’s Once Upon a Time in Harlem . The project restores old, unreleased footage shot by William, which his son, David, helped assemble and spruce up for a new generation to understand. William Greaves, who died in 2014, was a former actor who, dispirited by the opportunities afforded him in postwar Hollywood, became a challenging, acclaimed filmmaker. His body of work is well worth a deep dive, particularly the avant-garde documentary Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One , which is itself about the reality-warping process of making documentaries. Once Upon a Time in Harlem , however, was left unfinished for decades. The documentary captures a party the elder Greaves threw in August 1972, bringing together every living member of the Harlem Renaissance he could find to Duke Ellington’s townhouse. He let the cameras roll as the group chatted, caroused, and unfurled memories of that flourishing era for Black art. David, then age 26, helped his father with the filming; more than 50 years later, he went through 60,000 feet of footage to pick out the best moments. The result is a rather stunning look back at an event filled with people who were already looking back; it’s a beautiful echo of an echo. Once Upon a Time in Harlem is debuting in select cinemas, but it’s a must-see—and will hopefully expand soon. What Else I’m Watching Chris Rock’s Misty Green received a mixed reception at this fall’s festivals, but it’s somewhat redeemed by Rosalind Eleazar’s lead performance. She plays a fading actress striving for a role while her personal life disintegrates around her, and her masterful on-screen sloppiness helps explain away some of the dodgier plot twists. I’ve always found Rock’s directorial career frustrating; although he has good taste and influences (this film has major Safdie-brothers energy), he always falls a little short of what he’s imitating. Criterion’s humongous Stanley Kubrick box set will finally be on shelves Tuesday, and it’s an unsurprisingly impressive package from those doyens of physical media. All 13 of his features have received sparkly restorations, and the collection also includes his daughter Vivian’s documentary Making The Shining , which offers a glimpse into the much-mythologized auteur’s process. The rare international version of The Shining , which is far shorter than the U.S. theatrical cut, is one of the best Easter eggs on offer. Another movie that had long been thought lost is the director’s cut of Ken Russell’s intense psychological horror The Devils , which was censored and outright banned in many countries on its 1971 release. The original version was officially unavailable for years, but a 4K restoration of it is now touring theaters. A 17th-century-set dramatization of witch-hunting within the French Catholic church, The Devils is genuinely shocking—especially given the era of its release—but should be required viewing for genre completionists.

items.title: Terrorism: Court jails 2 for life for assisting Boko Haram members
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced two men to life imprisonment for providing support to members of the proscribed Boko Haram terrorist group. The convicts, Abba Mustapha and Bukar Ibrahim, both from Borno State, were arrested by the Department of State Services (DSS). Trial Justice Salim Ibrahim handed down the sentence after the duo pleaded guilty to the charge the Federal Government preferred against them. The Federal Government alleged that, aside from aiding the operations of insurgents, the convicts also concealed information about their whereabouts. While they received life imprisonment on the first count of the charge, the court sentenced them to 20 years on the second count. The judgment followed the resumption of another phase of the mass trial of alleged terrorists and their facilitators by the Federal Government. No fewer than 59 suspects were listed to appear before various judges of the court. Some of the judges presiding over the cases include Justices Ibrahim, James Omotosho, Binta Nyako, Emeka Nwite, Obiora Egwuatu, Hauwa Yilwa, Joyce Abdulmalik and Peter Lifu. It will be recalled that in June, the Federal Government prosecuted over 600 individuals allegedly affiliated with terrorist organisations. The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, said the exercise was meant to send a clear message that the administration is not treating terrorism with levity. items.title: L’association « Nous sommes la solution » appelle les Etats à investir sur la femme rurale
items.description: La journée de la femme rurale a mobilisé plusieurs femmes dans la commune de Sédhiou. Cette rencontre tenue ce 15 octobre 2026 a été un prétexte pour la présidente de « Nous sommes la solution », une organisation agroécologique panafricaine, de plaider pour le soutien des activités agricoles des femmes rurales. SEDHIOU- L'ambiance était au rendez-vous ce jeudi 15 octobre, sur la place de l’indépendance de la région de Sédhiou où plusieurs femmes venues de différents horizons ont célébré la journée internationale de la femme rurale. Cette rencontre a permis de mettre en exergue le rôle de la femme dans la production agroécologique. « Si aujourd’hui on parle de l’agroécologie, c’est grâce au travail inlassable des femmes rurales dans l’agriculture vivrière », estime Mariama Sonko, présidente du mouvement panafricain « nous sommes la solution ». Rappelant que cette agroécologie est basée sur le savoir et savoir-faire que les ancêtres ont transmis depuis des générations. La présidente l’association nous sommes la solution a aussi a loué la bravoure et le mérite de la femme rurale. « Aujourd’hui, investir dans cette couche de femme, c’est investir sur l’ensemble de la population africaine », a-t-assumé. Cette année, la journée de la femme rurale est célébrée autour de : « L’émancipation des femmes : construire un avenir résilient avec Beijing+30. Investir dans la femme rurale : un levier pour la croissance économique et le développement durable ». Ce thème est un prétexte, pour Mme Sonko de rappeler la doléance de son association. « Depuis 2011 nous plaidons pour que l’Etat investisse sur cette pratique agroécologie dont détiennent les femmes rurales. Malheureusement, ils sont toujours rués sur l’autre pratique qui détruit notre agriculture », regrette-elle. La santé de l’environnement aussi bien que celle des êtres vivants est menacée par cette forme d’agriculture. L’association « Nous sommes la solution », est présente Bénin, du Burkina Faso, de la Côte d’Ivoire, de la Gambie, du Ghana, de la Guinée, de la Guinée-Bissau, du Mali, de la Mauritanie, du Niger, du Sénégal et du Togo. Elle réunit en son sein 800 associations de femmes rurales regroupant plus de 200 000 membres et sympathisants. Jonas Souloubany BASSENE (correspondant)

items.title: This Is Edgar Allan Poe, and I Am Begging Kelly Clarkson to Take My Bird
items.description: Dear Kelly Clarkson, Miss Clarkson. I have read that you wanted a bird but were not permitted to obtain it. Well, I am in possession of a bird and do not want to be. Perhaps we could come to a mutually beneficial arrangement. In brief: There is a bird in here. Specifically, a raven. It sits, croaking, uninvited, on my bust of Pallas. (I would also be happy to give you the bust of Pallas. It is a tasteful bust; my only qualm with it is that it reminds me of my lost Lenore.) I didn’t ask the bird to be here. To the contrary, I would like nothing more than for it to depart. I have asked it to do so, first politely, and then rudely. But nothing. The raven will not budge. When I read of your encounter with the store Art of Play I felt the only hint of hope I had felt for quite some time. I thought: This woman needs a bird. I have a bird. I will tell her the situation, and we can wring some triumph out of this whole miserable thing. How did I come by this bird? Oh, the usual way. I’m sure you know the feeling. It’s a midnight dreary. You’re pondering, weak and weary, many and many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore. You are thinking of your lost Lenore. Then you hear a tapping, as of someone gently rapping, rapping at your chamber door? Well, this happened to me recently. But it wasn’t someone. It was a bird. And now the accursed thing will not depart! I want to be rid of the bird. And you want a bird. I understand that the bird in which you expressed interest is a windup bird. Well, this raven certainly winds me up. Is that anything? I understand that the bird in which you were interested is named Molly. My raven could be named Molly. You could call it anything if only you would take the demonic thing out of here! Before you object that the kind of bird you want is inanimate, whereas mine is clearly a live bird, I have considered this, and I think that the main objection people have to a live bird indoors is that the bird will fly around disruptively and try to escape. Well, the raven does not do that. I wish it would. I have opened the casement. I have said, “Shoo, bird.” I have said sterner things, things that I now regret. But the raven does not budge. It just sits there and says, “Nevermore,” at intervals. Also, its sable hue would go with anything. Looking at this bird from an interior-design perspective, I think it would fit any room, especially if I included the bust, which, again, I am willing to do. Do you need to feed it? I have not gotten that far with the bird. So far, it has not eaten anything. I think maybe it sustains itself by other means. It just sits there saying, “Nevermore.” Make no mistake, I am not offering you a free bird because I doubt your ability to pay. I am offering you a bird because I hate the infernal creature and want it out of my sight! But I would accept your money. Using that money, I could perhaps even get rid of the beating heart that seems to be stuck in my wall. I eagerly await your response. Sincerely, EAP

items.title: JOJ « DAKAR 2026 »: Finitions, budget, héritage… Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye lève le voile
items.description: À deux semaines de l’ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, prévue le 31 octobre à 17 heures à Diamniadio, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, président du comité d’organisation, a détaillé dans un entretien avec Le Soleil à paraître ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 dans l’édition print, l’état des préparatifs, le financement et les ambitions de ces premiers Joj organisés en Afrique. Dans quinze jours, sera donné le coup d’envoi des Joj Dakar 2026. L’heure n’est plus donc aux grands chantiers, mais aux finitions. C’est le message central livré par le président du Comité d’organisation des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse (Cojoj), Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, dans une interview exclusive à lire dans la version papier du Soleil de ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026. Évaluant l'état d'avancement général à 92 %, il insiste sur une « confiance active » pour régler le « dernier kilomètre » : la synchronisation des transports, l'accréditation des volontaires, la logistique et l'approvisionnement en eau sur tous les sites. « Le 31 octobre à 17 heures, à Diamniadio, le Sénégal accueillera le monde. Nous ne promettons pas des Jeux parfaits, mais des Jeux authentiques, à la hauteur de la Téranga sénégalaise », a laissé entendre le président du Cnoss. Lire aussi: JOJ Dakar 2026 : après les infrastructures, le pari de la mobilisation populaire Interrogé sur la remise récente de plusieurs infrastructures clés par le chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye y voit un acte fort de souveraineté nationale. Le Village des Jeux à Diamniadio, le stade Iba-Mar-Diop rénové ou encore la piscine olympique intègrent désormais le patrimoine pérenne du pays. Pour éviter le piège des « éléphants blancs », le Cojoj, selon lui, s'est aligné sur les exigences de sobriété et de durabilité du Comité international olympique (Cio). C’est-à-dire sobriété et réhabilitation (à Diamniadio, le Cojoj a privilégié la rénovation à la construction neuve) ; reconversion garantie (le Village des Jeux deviendra un campus universitaire dès la fin de la compétition) et modèle économique (l’entretien des sites est confié à l’Agence de gestion du patrimoine bâti, avec des crédits d'ores et déjà provisionnés dans la loi de finances). Un budget présenté comme sécurisé et public Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye affirme que le budget est sécurisé à 100 % et public. Il dément les chiffres de 80 milliards de Fcfa avancés par certains. Il précise que le budget opérationnel du Cojoj s’élève à 32 milliards de Fcfa, financés à 60 % par le Cio et ses partenaires. Le reste correspond aux investissements de l’État (routes, eau, stades), qui resteront au pays. Lire aussi: Vidéo: D’Athènes à Dakar, le voyage des « Argonautes » sénégalais Bien que les compétitions soient concentrées entre Dakar, Diamniadio et Saly, l’événement se veut national. Le Cojoj a déployé un vaste dispositif d'animation territoriale impliquant 45 collectivités, 300 associations Navétanes et 12 000 écoles, appuyé par une billetterie accessible à 1 000 FCFA pour les clubs et scolaires. La tournée de la flamme olympique à travers les capitales régionales – portée par des figures du sport sénégalais comme Brancou Badio, Oumy Diop, Louis François Mendy, Fary Seye ou Ousseynou Diop – a confirmé l'engouement populaire. L’Afrique au cœur du mouvement olympique Pendant 130 ans, l'Afrique est restée spectatrice des Jeux. Pour Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye, la responsabilité confiée au Sénégal dépasse largement ses frontières : il s'agit d'organiser l'événement au nom des 54 pays du continent. Le succès de Dakar 2026 doit ouvrir la voie à de futures candidatures africaines pour les Jeux Olympiques de 2036 ou 2040, estime-t-il. Sur le plan sportif et humain, la dimension continentale s'incarne directement. Sur le terrain, plus de 800 athlètes africains prendront part aux épreuves. Dans l'organisation, 400 jeunes professionnels issus de 30 pays africains sont intégrés au sein de la Learning Academy, véritable cœur de transmission des compétences d'organisation événementielle. Lire aussi: Le Président de la République appelle à imprimer un cachet populaire aux JOJ Dakar 2026 Pour le président du Cojoj, au-delà des médailles, l'objectif affiché est de susciter des vocations et de multiplier par trois l'accès des jeunes sénégalais à des infrastructures sportives modernes. Pour mesurer l'impact réel à long terme, un Observatoire de l’Héritage a été mis en place en collaboration avec l’Ansd et l’Ucad, afin d'évaluer chaque année le taux d'utilisation des sites, le nombre de licenciés et la formation des jeunes. Revenant sur le report des Jeux en 2020 dû à la pandémie de Covid-19 – un moment perçu initialement comme un coup dur -, Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye conclut qu'il s'est transformé en opportunité pour parfaire l'organisation. Son invitation finale s'adresse directement au public : « Venez le 31 octobre. Ne regardez pas Dakar 2026 à la télévision : vivez ces Jeux ! » Par Elhadj Ibrahima THIAM et Samba Oumar FALL Retrouvez l’intégralité de cet entretien dans Le Soleil du vendredi 16 octobre 2026.

items.title: Senate orders probe into corps member’s death at Enugu NYSC camp
items.description: The Senate has ordered an investigation into the death of a National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) member, Etimbuk Daniel, at the Enugu State orientation camp, amid concerns over medical facilities and emergency response services in camps nationwide. The resolution, adopted on Thursday, followed a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Senator Aniekan Bassey, who called for an urgent review of healthcare services available to corps members across the country. The investigation will be conducted by the Senate Committees on Police Affairs, Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, Ethics, Code of Conduct and Public Petitions, Youth Development and Health, in conjunction with the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services. The probe is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding Daniel’s death and determine whether any lapses occurred in the provision of medical care at the camp. Bassey expressed concern over “the sudden and untimely passing of the corps member, describing him as a vibrant, patriotic young Nigerian and a shining light of his community who had only set out to serve the country.” He said the incident raised broader questions about the adequacy of medical services available to corps members participating in the mandatory national service programme. “The incident is not isolated, but highlights a recurring pattern of systemic negligence, poor medical infrastructure, and absence of qualified emergency personnel and rapid referral protocols across NYSC camps, underlining that the government owes a duty of care to young graduates mobilized away from their homes to serve the nation.” The senator said Daniel had embarked on national service with hopes of contributing to Nigeria’s development before his death. He called for urgent legislative scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly allegations of medical negligence, inadequate healthcare infrastructure and ineffective emergency response and referral systems at orientation camps. Citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, Bassey said the security and welfare of the people remained the primary purpose of government. He argued that the government and relevant authorities had a responsibility to protect corps members and ensure they received timely and adequate medical care throughout their service year. Bassey added that Daniel’s death had thrown his family, associates, the student community and the people of Akwa Ibom State into mourning, stressing the need for a thorough investigation. The Senate Chief Whip, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, representing Borno North, seconded the motion. Contributing to the debate, Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, expressed condolences to Daniel’s family, Bassey and the people of Akwa Ibom State and Nigeria. Ningi urged the relevant committees to make concrete recommendations and identify measures to prevent similar incidents in the future. The Senate subsequently observed a minute of silence in honour of the deceased. Daniel, the immediate past Students’ Union Government president of Akwa Ibom State University, reportedly died at the NYSC orientation camp in Enugu State following allegations that he was given fake medication and did not receive timely medical attention. Reports indicated that Daniel complained of a headache at the camp and was given medication, but his condition allegedly deteriorated afterwards. items.title: 50 houses razed, scores injured as explosion rocks Rivers community
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor About 20 people have been injured and over 50 houses burnt down following the explosion of a gas pipeline in Aleto community, Eleme Local Government Area of Rivers State. The incident, which happened Thursday, occurred around 5pm occured from an alleged ruptured pipeline belonging to the Nigeria Gas Company along the Old Bori Road in Aleto. A source, who is a resident of the area, narrated: “The Pipeline has caused injuries and damaged properties. This pipeline has been leaking for about three weeks before the explosion today.” The source gave his name as Emmanuel said some leaders of the area have notified the company about the leak but the company did not respond positively. Leader of the Eleme Legislative Council, Daniel Chuma, said he had written to the company about the leak and followed up with a petition to relevant authorities but nothing concrete was done to stop the gas leak. Chuma, who visited the scene of the explosion, said: “There was a leakage on another section of the Nigeria Gas Company. We wrote to them, and we did a petition to NOSDRA and Rivers State Ministry of Environment and copied the Police for urgent intervention. “We asked for a joint investigation. We don’t know what they did before they left. Today we were called to an explosion at the same pipeline of the Nigeria Gas Company that has destroyed over 50 houses, cars, and many casualties. People have been rushed to the hospital. “Before now, everyone scampered for safety. The few that came, we asked them to stay far away to avoid any further incident.” Meanwhile, the Executive Director of the Youths and Environmental Advocacy Centre, YEAC-Nigeria, Dr Fyneface Dumnamene, in a statement, confirmed the development. Fyneface said: “We are using this medium to call on the relevant authorities, the Rivers State government, Ministry of Environment, NOSDRA, the Rivers State, the Federal Government, and all the bodies involved in checking oil spill and explosion to come to the aid of Aleto people. This is a serious incident. “As of the time of this statement, YEAC-Nigeria has not independently confirmed any fatalities. “Members of the Advocacy Centre’s volunteers who visited the scene for independent verification confirmed the presence of officials of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on ground. The cause of the incident is yet to be independently verified. “YEAC-Nigeria calls on the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) to identify the facility operator and conduct a Joint Investigation Visit to the site, and to invoke relevant provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021 as appropriate,” he added. items.title: Tinubu orders security chiefs to rescue abductees, guarantee safe elections
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has directed heads of security agencies to ensure a safe and secure environment for Nigerians to vote freely in the elections scheduled for January, Minister of Defence General Christopher Musa (retd) has said. The minister disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents after a security meeting presided over by the President at Aso Villa, Abuja. He said the session was convened to update Tinubu on the security situation across the country ahead of the polls. “Today’s meeting was to brief Mr. President on the security situation within the country. You know, the elections coming in January, and it’s important that we keep him abreast of what is ongoing,” the minister said. Gen. Musa said all heads of security agencies attended the “intensive discussion,” during which the President made clear his expectation for the electoral process. “Mr. President made it very clear he wants a free, fair, and credible election. We must do everything possible to ensure that the country is safe and secure for the citizens to go out and vote,” Musa stated. The minister assured Nigerians that the security forces would remain neutral and would not allow intimidation of voters or political actors. “We are going to ensure that we give everybody opportunity to go and serve, so they have nothing to worry about, nothing to be afraid of, and that nobody is going to intimidate them for whatever reasons,” he said. “It is important for all other political parties to ensure to understand that the security forces are going to be neutral.” The Defence Minister also dismissed suggestions that underage persons were being recruited into the armed forces, saying the concern related to terrorists’ use of children. According to him, “There is nobody that is underage that is being brought here. I think the discussion that was made was that the accusation was on the terrorists using underage. “Well, we know that we don’t have control over what they do, and that’s why it’s important for us to understand that we must not allow them remain wherever they are.” He said the President had ordered security agencies to intensify operations to locate abducted persons and dismantle terrorist and bandit enclaves. “The directive from the president is: all of us must go all out to fish out and rescue all those that have been abducted, kidnapped wherever they are. There shouldn’t be any camp of any terrorists or bandits anywhere in Nigeria,” Musa declared. On measures to improve security capacity, the minister cited increased recruitment, training, and procurement. He said the President would soon commission “almost about 10” newly acquired aircraft and helicopters. “Mr. President is coming to commission a set of new aircrafts and helicopters that have been bought. I think almost about 10 of them in number, and to show Nigerians that despite the economic issue, the issue of security is in the front burner of Mr. President’s view,” he said. The minister also pointed to the recent salary increment for members of the armed forces, adding that improvements for the police, other agencies, and pensioners were being addressed. “I’m sure very soon the police and all others is being been addressed, including those of the pensioners. Nobody is going to be left behind,” he said. The minister urged citizens to support security agencies by reporting wrongdoing, including misconduct by security personnel. “Security is everybody’s responsibility. It’s not only for members of security forces. Everyone has a role to play,” he said. “Whatever you see that is going wrong, even with our members that are not doing what is right, please don’t hesitate to report. Action will be taken.” The high-level meeting was attended by the National Security Adviser, NSA, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Minister of Police Affairs, Senator Ibrahim Gaidam; Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle; and Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka Famadewa (rtd.). Also in attendance were the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu; Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas; Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke; and Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lieutenant General Emmanuel Undiandeye. Other security chiefs at the meeting included the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu; Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency (NIA), Ambassador Mohammed Mohammed; and Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi. The post Tinubu orders security chiefs to rescue abductees, guarantee safe elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Abusive Care Facility in Thailand Raises Broader Concerns
items.description: Click to expand Image A person lies in bed at a nursing home in Ayutthaya, Thailand, April 9, 2016. © 2016 Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters A care facility in Kanchanaburi, Thailand made headlines in early October when photos of conditions in the facility went viral, including images allegedly depicting metal cages that confine residents to their beds. Further investigation by the country’s Department of Health Service Support uncovered unsanitary conditions and overcrowding, as well as evidence that the facility had been treating residents with psychosocial disabilities (mental health conditions) without an appropriate license. The whistleblower, known as “Mae Phat,” appeared on television to recount her experiences at Sothornchai Nursing Home as a former resident, describing how she was involuntarily committed, forced to take medication, and physically restrained, often for hours at a time. Thai officials promptly ordered the facility’s closure as well as inspections of 1,203 facilities for older people nationwide. While the authorities have taken appropriate first steps, conditions at the facility have raised broader concerns about institutionalization, shackling, and the treatment of older people in Thailand. The United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs predicts that 28 percent of Thailand's population will be 65 or older within the next decade. Though Thailand has launched a community-based long-term care program for older people, responsibility for care falls under several government ministries. Ongoing shortages of qualified care and support workers as well as budgetary constraints leave many older people reliant on family care, which not all families can adequately provide. The Thai government should take this opportunity to reconsider its fragmented policies and commit to ensuring older people are treated with dignity and empowered to make decisions about their care and support. The government should develop and implement a comprehensive, time-bound deinstitutionalization plan for older people and people with disabilities, ensuring full access to community-based services and individualized support that would enable them to live independently and participate fully in their communities. The government should also establish a task force to conduct regular, unannounced visits to public and private institutions housing older people and people with psychosocial disabilities, assessing living conditions and conducting confidential interviews with residents and staff. This task force should also establish a hotline to receive and investigate reports of abuse and ensure accountability. Thailand should move beyond institutional care and guarantee everyone the support required to live independently in the community.

items.title: ‘He slipped, knocked head in bathroom’ – Ningi recounts Senator Mandiya’s death
items.description: The Senator representing Bauchi Central, Abdul Ningi, has recounted the circumstances surrounding the death of his late colleague, Bello Mandiya, who reportedly slipped and hit his head in his bathroom, with his body discovered about 72 hours later at his Abuja residence. Ningi narrated the incident during Senate plenary on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. A video of his account went viral on Thursday. According to Ningi, Mandiya lived alone, and his absence went unnoticed for days until the chief imam of Apo became concerned that the former lawmaker had missed prayers for three consecutive days. Ningi said he was in Saudi Arabia when his son called to inform him of Mandiya’s death. His son was among those who discovered the former senator’s body on September 7, 2026. Recounting the events leading to the discovery, Ningi said Mandiya was last seen by a colleague at about 11 am on Friday, September 4, after returning home to prepare for the congregational prayer. “He brought out his cap, his phones, and put them on the bed, and went into the bathroom to take his bath. “After taking his bath, when he was out of the bathroom, then he slipped and knocked his head in the bathroom,” Ningi said. The senator explained that the incident remained unknown until a foul smell began emanating from Mandiya’s apartment, raising concerns among residents. “For 72 hours, Mr President, nobody knew where Bello Mandiya was,” he said. Ningi said those who went to the residence eventually forced the door open and found the former lawmaker dead in the bathroom. “And there lies Bello Mandiya in the bathroom, lifeless. Seventy-two hours, and that’s a simple tragedy,” he said. Reflecting on the incident, Ningi said Mandiya’s death underscored the uncertainty of life, stressing that political positions and material wealth offered no guarantee against tragedy. “There is nothing permanent about anything. Nothing permanent about our position, nothing permanent about our wealth,” Ningi said. The senator, who said he had known Mandiya since 2002, offered prayers for the deceased and extended his condolences to his family, the people of Katsina State and his former constituents. items.title: Rebondissement dans l’affaire Dr Diané : Charles Wright se pourvoit en cassation contre l’arrêt en appel
items.description: La bataille judiciaire entre le parquet spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF) et l’ancien ministre de la Défense nationale, Dr Mohamed Diané, est loin d’être terminée. Le procureur spécial, Alphonse Charles Wright, a annoncé son intention de se pourvoir en cassation contre l’arrêt rendu par la chambre des appels, dont il conteste les motifs juridiques. Face à la presse, le chef du parquet spécial a indiqué que cette démarche ne visait pas la personne de l’ancien ministre, mais plutôt ce qu’il considère comme une mauvaise interprétation du droit par les magistrats ayant rendu la décision. « Le parquet est formellement en pourvoi contre l’arrêt qui vient d’être rendu par la chambre des appels de la CRIEF. Cette décision, ce n’est pas contre la personne de Dr Diané, c’est la mauvaise interprétation du droit qui a été faite », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Alphonse Charles Wright, la contestation porte essentiellement sur le raisonnement juridique ayant conduit à cet arrêt. Il entend ainsi soumettre les arguments du ministère public à l’appréciation de la Cour suprême. Revenant sur la procédure, le procureur spécial a rappelé que Dr Diané avait été reconnu coupable en première instance de détournement de deniers publics, d’enrichissement illicite et de blanchiment de capitaux. Il a notamment insisté sur la responsabilité des gestionnaires publics dans la justification de l’utilisation des fonds mis à leur disposition. « Il revient à l’ordonnateur des dépenses de justifier l’exécution de ses dépenses », a-t-il soutenu, estimant que l’ancien ministre n’aurait pas apporté les justifications nécessaires concernant l’utilisation des fonds publics concernés. Le procureur spécial a également soulevé des interrogations sur l’appréciation des faits liés à la commande publique, notamment sur la portée du procès-verbal de réception dans l’examen des éventuelles irrégularités. « Comment peut-on dire que les règles du marché public n’ont pas été violées, par le seul motif qu’il y ait un procès-verbal de réception ? », a-t-il lancé, estimant que l’existence d’un tel document ne saurait, à elle seule, suffire à écarter d’éventuels manquements aux règles de passation des marchés publics. Dans son intervention, Alphonse Charles Wright a, par ailleurs, insisté sur l’obligation de rendre compte qui incombe aux gestionnaires des deniers publics. Il a rappelé que le ministère public avait pour mission de défendre les intérêts de la société guinéenne, tout en veillant au respect des droits des personnes poursuivies devant la juridiction. Le chef du parquet spécial a toutefois réaffirmé son désaccord avec les motifs retenus par la chambre des appels. « Je ne discute pas ce qui a été dit, mais je conteste les motifs légaux qui ont été avancés. […] Je ne peux être convaincu ni par la teneur ni par la forme selon laquelle cette décision a été rendue », a-t-il affirmé. En conclusion, Alphonse Charles Wright a prévenu que le différend judiciaire avec l’ancien ministre était loin d’être clos. « Dr Diané doit savoir que la bataille avec le parquet n’est pas terminée et c’est loin de finir », a-t-il averti. Le pourvoi annoncé ouvre ainsi une nouvelle étape dans cette affaire. Il reviendra désormais à la Cour suprême d’examiner les moyens de droit soulevés par le parquet spécial contre l’arrêt de la chambre des appels de la CRIEF.

items.title: ONU : le Maroc vote pour une résolution soutenant l’autodétermination du peuple sahraoui
items.description: Nouvelle grande victoire pour la cause sahraouie devant les institutions internationales. La quatrième commission de l’Assemblée générale de l’ ONU a adopté ce jeudi 15 octobre un projet de résolution sur la question du Sahara occidental, réaffirmant le droit inaliénable du peuple sahraoui à l’autodétermination, conformément aux principes onusiens relatifs à la décolonisation. La résolution a été votée également par la délégation marocaine, rapporte l’agence APS . Réaffirmation du caractère de question de décolonisation du conflit sahraoui Cette adoption équivaut à la réaffirmation du caractère de « question de décolonisation inachevée » du conflit sahraoui. Le projet de résolution a été adopté à une écrasante majorité. Il a été examiné dans le cadre des travaux de la commission chargée des questions politiques spéciales et de la décolonisation. La résolution réaffirme le droit inaliénable du peuple sahraoui à l’autodétermination, conformément aux principes consacrés par la Charte des Nations unies et aux résolutions pertinentes de l’Assemblée générale, notamment la résolution 1514 du 14 décembre 1960 portant Déclaration sur l’octroi de l’indépendance aux pays et aux peuples coloniaux. Cette adoption « consacre le cadre onusien de la question du Sahara occidental en tant que question de décolonisation inachevée, nécessitant de permettre au peuple sahraoui d’exercer son droit à l’autodétermination, conformément aux principes du droit international et aux résolutions pertinentes des Nations unies », écrit l’ APS . Lâché par ses alliés, le Maroc a voté « oui » Selon la même source, le vote a recueilli le soutien de 152 États membres, ce qui souligne « l’importance du respect de la légalité internationale et des engagements des Nations unies en matière de décolonisation, ainsi que le rejet de toute approche susceptible de contourner le droit fondamental des peuples sous domination coloniale à choisir librement leur avenir politique ». L’occupant marocain a lui-même été contraint de voter en faveur du projet de résolution, alors que sa délégation envisageait initialement de s’abstenir de participer au vote. « Face à l’ampleur du soutien exprimé par les États membres, y compris certains de ses alliés, le Maroc a finalement rejoint les voix favorables au texte », indique l’ APS. Après le vote, un responsable du Front Polisario a estimé que la réaffirmation du cadre juridique du Sahara occidental en tant que question de décolonisation constitue une réponse « forte et claire » aux tentatives de l’occupant marocain de déformer la nature juridique de la question sahraouie. Une réponse « forte et claire » au Maroc Sidi Mohamed Ammar, représentant du Front Polisario auprès de l’ONU et coordonnateur avec la MINURSO, a dénoncé, dans une déclaration aux médias, les tentatives du Maroc visant à promouvoir des allégations trompeuses devant la quatrième commission de l’Assemblée générale, en mobilisant un groupe de mercenaires et d’agents pour relayer sa propagande mensongère, ainsi que le recours à l’intimidation verbale au sein de cette instance onusienne. Dans un autre registre, le groupe de Genève de soutien au Sahara occidental a appelé, lors de la 77e session du Comité exécutif du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR), à la nécessité de parvenir à « une solution politique juste et durable au conflit du Sahara occidental, conformément aux buts et principes de la Charte des Nations unies ». Cet appel est intervenu dans un communiqué lu par le représentant permanent du Mozambique auprès du bureau des Nations unies à Genève, Geraldo Gonçalves Miguel, au nom du groupe, qui réunit un nombre important de pays africains, asiatiques et d’Amérique latine soutenant le droit du peuple sahraoui à l’autodétermination. L’article ONU : le Maroc vote pour une résolution soutenant l’autodétermination du peuple sahraoui est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: La dura negociación sobre el presupuesto de la UE amenaza el acuerdo antes del superaño electoral en Europa
items.description: La pelea sobre el presupuesto que va a marcar las políticas de la UE en los próximos siete años se está encarnizando . Las discrepancias entre los llamados frugales, con Alemania a la cabeza, que abogan por el tijeretazo, y los amigos de la cohesión , entre ellos, España e Italia, que piden más dinero, amenazan con encallar un acuerdo sobre el marco financiero plurianual antes de final de año. Todo ello, en un clima políticamente muy tenso y en vísperas de un superaño electoral que, en realidad, se adelanta con los comicios de noviembre en España. “Honestamente, no tenemos prisa. Los ciudadanos suecos no son el cajero automático de la UE”, ha lanzado el primer ministro sueco, Ulf Kristersson, que aboga por el hachazo al presupuesto, este jueves en Bruselas. “Estamos con una propuesta claramente insuficiente”, ha advertido, por su parte, el presidente español, Pedro Sánchez. items.title: Santé : La « Medleaders association » mobilise les jeunes professionnels de la santé contre le cancer du sein
items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP) – La MedLeaders Association (MLA) a lancé, le jeudi 15 octobre à Lomé, le MLA Health Summit 2026, une rencontre scientifique destinée à mobiliser les jeunes professionnels de la santé autour des enjeux de prévention, de sensibilisation et de dépistage précoce du cancer du sein. La rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre de la célébration des dix années d’existence du MLA et d’« Octobre Rose », mois dédié à la sensibilisation au cancer du sein. Cette rencontre est meublée de panels, de conférences scientifiques, d’ateliers, d’expositions et de stands. Des activités de sensibilisation sont également prévues à l’endroit des élèves, des jeunes filles et des femmes. La MLA Health Summit 2026 ambitionne aussi de favoriser les échanges d’expériences et de renforcer les relations professionnelles entre les acteurs du secteur sanitaire, dans l’optique d’une meilleure implication des jeunes dans la lutte contre cette maladie. Intervenant au nom du ministre chargé de la Santé, le professeur Bello Mofou a souligné une grave prolifération de cette maladie chez les femmes. Il a indiqué que le cancer du sein figure parmi les principales causes de mortalité féminine, d’où la nécessité de renforcer les actions de prévention, de sensibilisation et de dépistage précoce. Pour sa part, le professeur Douaguibe, représentant le doyen de la Faculté des sciences de la santé, a insisté sur l’importance de rapprocher les actions de sensibilisation des populations. Il a appelé à intensifier les campagnes d’information dans les maisons, les quartiers et sur les lieux de culte, afin de toucher un public plus large et d’encourager les femmes à s’intéresser davantage à leur santé. La représentante de la MedLeaders Association, Djibare Wake a mis en avant l’engagement de l’association en faveur de la prévention des maladies non transmissibles et de la promotion de la santé. « À travers ce sommet, l’organisation entend offrir un cadre d’échanges scientifiques aux jeunes professionnels de la santé pour réfléchir aux défis liés au cancer du sein et proposer des approches de solutions sur la base d’un diagnostic précoce », a expliqué Mme Djibaré. Créée il y a dix ans, la MedLeaders Association rassemble de jeunes professionnels de la santé autour d’initiatives visant notamment la prévention des maladies non transmissibles et la promotion de la santé. items.title: FILDAK : après sept ans d’absence, Dakar redevient la capitale du livre
items.description: Sept ans. Il aura fallu sept ans pour que la Foire internationale du livre et du matériel didactique de Dakar (FILDAK) retrouve son public. Ce jeudi, au Centre international du commerce extérieur du Sénégal (CICES), le monde du livre s'est retrouvé pour lancer sa 18e édition. La foire se tient jusqu'au 19 octobre. Une soixantaine d'exposants venus de plus de dix pays y participent, avec l'Égypte comme invitée d'honneur. Le thème : « Bibliothèque, transmission et souveraineté ». L'ambition affichée : faire de Dakar « le cœur palpitant du livre ». Si la foire s'était tue pendant sept ans, c'est en grande partie à cause de la Covid-19. Son retour, la ministre en charge de la culture des industries créative et du patrimoine historique, Mame Coumba Diop, l'avait salué dès le 5 octobre, à l'occasion de la présentation de la programmation, comme « un signal fort pour la culture et l'éducation ». Née en 1985, la FILDAK a toujours poursuivi les mêmes objectifs : renforcer les réseaux de diffusion du livre, mettre en relation tous les maillons de la chaîne, créer une solidarité entre les professionnels, promouvoir le livre et le matériel didactique, faire rayonner la culture du Sénégal et de l'Afrique, et défendre la diversité culturelle. À l'ouverture, présidée par le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, le gouvernement a réaffirmé sa ligne. « Le gouvernement maintiendra le livre au cœur de sa politique culturelle », a promis le chef du gouvernement, en ajoutant que « la Bibliothèque nationale et la Maison des archives seront réalisées ». Il s'est aussi arrêté sur le thème de l'édition, qu'il voit comme une invitation à une « réflexion profonde » sur la place de la bibliothèque et de la lecture. À ses yeux, une bibliothèque n'est ni un simple bâtiment ni une collection d'ouvrages. Elle traduit la volonté collective de rassembler, d'organiser et de partager les savoirs, les mémoires et l'imaginaire qui fondent une civilisation. Quant à l'Égypte, son choix comme invitée d'honneur n'a rien du hasard. « Mère d'édition de notre espace régional », elle est liée à l'Afrique subsaharienne, et au Sénégal en particulier, par « de profondes continuités culturelles », a rappelé le Premier ministre, évoquant une civilisation millénaire. Pour lui, ce choix traduit un rapprochement scientifique et culturel entre les deux peuples, une amitié ancienne, mais aussi une diplomatie solide. Du côté égyptien, le vice-ministre de la Culture, Oumar Sélim, a rappelé que son pays fut le premier pays africain aux côtés du Sénégal à l'aube de son indépendance. « Par le savoir, les peuples se rapprochent », a-t-il ajouté, citant l'Université Senghor comme témoignage de la solidarité entre les deux peuples. Mamadou Laye DIÈYE

items.title: Teacher, 30 students killed in Peshawar school roof collapse
items.description: PESHAWAR: At least 31 people, including 30 students and a female teacher, were killed when a school roof collapsed in the provincial capital’s Afridi Abad area on Thursday. Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) spokesperson Muhammad Asim initially told Dawn that the death toll had risen to 33, including a female teachers and students aged between seven and 14 and a female teacher. Later, he said that 30 students students and a female teacher had been killed. According to the official list of casualties shared by LRH, a total of 61 people were brought to the facility, of which 30 were discharged after being treated. Residents gather during a search operation after a roof collapsed at a school in Peshawar on October 15. —AFP A spokesman for Rewscue 1122 said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way. “When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside,” spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said. Speaking to Geo News , Peshawar Deputy Commissioner Afaq Wazir confirmed that the rescue operation launched after the collapse had concluded. “Rescue teams have cleared all the debris, and no more injured children are at the scene,” he said. Following the incident, an emergency was declared at the hospital, said the LRH spokesperson in an earlier statement. Peshawar DC earlier told Dawn that the roof of Al-Khair School had collapsed, trapping students beneath the debris. According to a statement issued by his office, students were present in their classrooms when the incident occurred. A rescue official told AFP that the ceiling came down on the students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two storeys. Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed said the building’s structure was weak. “Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse,” AFP quoted him as saying. A girl who was injured after a school roof collapse receives first aid at a hospital in Peshawar October 15, 2026. —AFP Speaking to Dawn , Samiullah, a parent who rushed to the site after hearing about the incident, said he had rescued three girls, all under the age of eight. “I received a call from home at around 8:50am and reached the site about 10 minutes later, at around 9am. We have six children studying at the school,” he said. “When I saw the building, I thought my son, who was in a ground-floor classroom beneath the collapsed first floor, had also died. However, he had left the classroom to drink water,” he added. Resident Sohail told AFP “everyone began screaming in panic” after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse. “When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said. Volunteers and relatives shift the body of a victim, killed after a roof collapsed at a school, into an ambulance outside a hospital in Peshawar on October 15, 2026. —AFP KP governor orders audit Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed grief over the deaths in the school roof collapse and sought a detailed report on the incident. He also directed the authorities to determine the cause of the collapse. “The loss of precious lives of innocent children is an extremely painful tragedy,” he said, according to a statement, extending his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. He prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured children and directed the authorities concerned to provide them with the best possible medical facilities. In another statement on his X account, the KP governor added that he had also directed a structural safety audit of educational institutions across the province to “identify potential risks and ensure that immediate corrective measures are taken wherever necessary”. “We cannot allow the safety of our children to be compromised,” Kundi wrote. Later, Kundi also attended the funeral prayers of the dead. Speaking to the media, he said that a team had been constituted to probe the incident and the inquiry was underway. “The first step will be to determine who issued the no-objection certificate to the school,” he said. Kundi also announced that the bereaved families would be given Rs1m as compensation while the injured would be given Rs200,000. “A transparent investigation into the incident will be conducted and those responsible will be identified,” he said. Late at night, a notification by the KP Human Resources Department said a fact-finding inquiry committee had been constituted to probe the incident. The committee is headed by Transport Department Secretary Zubair Ahmed and include Chief Engineer Jamshid Ali Khan of the Communication and Works Department. The terms of reference of the committee state that the body will: Conduct a detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the collapse of the classroom roof and establish the sequence of events Examine the structural condition of the building, quality of construction, maintenance history and compliance with applicable building safety requirements Determine the causes of the collapse and identify any negligence, lapses or responsibility on the part of individuals, school management or concerned regulatory authorities Examine the role of the concerned departments and regulatory bodies in ensuring the structural safety of the school building Recommend appropriate action against those found responsible, if any. Recommend practical preventive measures, including arrangements for structural safety inspections of government and private schools, to avoid recurrence of such incidents. “The committee may co-opt any technical expert, including structural engineer considered necessary and shall submit its report to the chief secretary within 7 days,” the notification said. Earlier, the Elementary and Secondary Education Department constituted a fact-finding committee to probe the incident and tasked it with submitting a report on Thursday. The committee included: Javid Iqbal, the chairman of the Private Schools Regularity Authority; Muhammad Farooq, the deputy secretary of the Elementary and Secondary Education Department; and a member to be co-opted by a committee. The committee was tasked with probing the incident and ascertaining the facts that led to the roof collapse, unearthing the factors that led to it, suggesting measures to prevent such incidents in the future and making appropriate recommendations. Separately, KP Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed ordered Peshawar CCPO to oversee the rescue operation and directed the traffic police to establish a “green corridor” to ensure uninterrupted movement of ambulances. Rescue and police teams were directed to utilise all available resources, a statement said. “In this hour of grief, KP police stands with the affected families,” the IGP was quoted as saying. Residents and rescue workers gather near an ambulance after a school roof collapse in Peshawar Pakistan on October 15.—Reuters PM Shehbaz takes ‘serious notice’ Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken “serious notice” of the incident, as he offered his condolences to the bereaved families in a post on X. “Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country,” DPM Dar said. He added that “ensuring the safety and protection of our children must remain paramount”. “All necessary measures must be taken to provide immediate assistance to those affected, ensure the best possible medical care for the injured, and strengthen safety standards in our schools to prevent such tragedies from recurring.” PM Shehbaz also phone the KP governor according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The prime minister offered condolences to the families of the deceased and directed authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to the injured and all possible assistance to the affected families, the statement said. The prime minister also sought a comprehensive report on the incident. The governor briefed the prime minister on the incident and informed him that the school owner had been arrested and an investigation into the incident had been launched. The prime minister directed that all aspects of the incident be examined and action be taken against those responsible in accordance with the law, the statement added. Condolences President Asif Ali Zardari also expressed “profound shock and grief” over the tragic school incident in a statement on X. “This heart-wrenching tragedy has plunged the entire nation into shock,” he said, extending his condolences to the families of the children killed. He directed relevant authorities to provide top-notch medical facilities to the injured and extend assistance to the affected families. “In this hour of sorrow, the entire nation shares equally in the grief of the affected families,” he said. President Zardari emphasised the need for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the incident and to ensure that all educational institutions’ buildings were following safety standards. PM Shehbaz expressed “deep grief and sorrow” over the incident, in a statement shared by his office. He extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured, directing that “all possible medical assistance” be provided. PM Shehbaz has also issued instructions to expedite relief operations, the statement said. In a post on X, he said: “My heart is with the families grieving the loss of their children and a teacher in the tragic roof collapse at a school in Peshawar. No parent should have to endure such pain. I extend my deepest condolences and pray for strength for every family affected.” He said that he had directed that the injured receive the best possible care. “We will ensure a thorough investigation into this tragedy and take every necessary step to protect the safety of children in schools across the country,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also expressed grief over the incident. In a post on X, he said he was “deeply saddened” by the tragedy, adding that the thought of parents sending their children to school in the morning only to receive news of their deaths was heartbreaking. He expressed solidarity with the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. Bilawal’s sister, MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari, also extended condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the swift recovery of the injured. She said schools must be places of learning and protection, adding that those responsible for ensuring children’s safety must be held accountable. Unicef also expressed its deep sadness over the incident. Unicef representative in Pakistan, Pernille Ironside, said in a statement: “Unicef extends its deepest condolences to the bereaved families and communities affected by this devastating incident.” “Our thoughts are also with the injured children; we wish them a swift and full recovery. Unicef stands ready to support the government’s response by providing psycho-social support to affected children, families and communities,” she said. Unicef called for urgent action to ensure that all schools, public and private, meet building safety standards and undergo regular safety inspections. “These standards must be strictly enforced to prevent such tragedies in future,” Ironside said. “Every child has the right to learn in a safe environment, where children can learn, grow and thrive, protected from harm. Going to school should never put a child’s life at risk,” she said. People stand near rubble after a school roof collapse in Peshawar, October 15, 2026. —Reuters The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) said it was “appalled” by the deaths. “It is important to stress that this was not an accident but a preventable failure, given that police have reportedly attributed the collapse to a weak structure carrying excessive construction,” it said, noting that a similar incident this year had killed 14 children at a tuition centre in Lahore. The commission called for an “independent, time-bound” inquiry with the findings to be made public. It also stressed the need for accountability of the school owner and the regulators “who allowed unsafe buildings to operate”, compensation for the families affected, and mandatory structural audits of all public and private schools. Roof collapse incidents Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, often attributed to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials. In July, three girls, aged 3 to 13, were killed after a portion of the outer wall of a government primary school near Umerkot collapsed and the rubble fell on them. The same month, a child died, and at least five other people were injured after the roof of an under-construction private school building collapsed in Lahore’s Baghbanpura neighbourhood . On June 30, 14 children lost their lives when the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. The incident had come less than two months after four children were killed and 20 people injured after the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan collapsed. A probe into the DG Khan incident revealed that construction for an extension of the tuition centre’s building was under way when the roof of the classroom collapsed. Last week, two men died in Pakpattan after the roof of their house collapsed during heavy rain and a windstorm. In June, a labourer was killed, and three others were injured when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed in Khawaspur locality of Lalamusa , Gujrat. The same month, two people were injured after the roof of a house collapsed in Lahore’s Nishtar area. In August, a couple was killed, and their daughters were injured after the roof of their house in Shahzad Town , Islamabad, collapsed following three days of heavy rainfall. Additional input from AFP

items.title: Procès d’Algassimou Diallo : la Cour suprême rejette les requêtes de la défense, qui suspend sa participation
items.description: Le procès d’Algassimou Diallo, ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême, poursuivi pour « provocation à la discrimination, à la haine ou à la violence, de la discrimination et association de malfaiteurs » et placé sous mandat de dépôt le jeudi 27 août 2026, s’est poursuivi ce jeudi 15 octobre devant la Cour suprême. L’audience du jour a été essentiellement consacrée à deux questions majeures : la demande de récusation de trois magistrats siégeant au sein des chambres réunies et la requête en annulation de l’ordonnance de renvoi de l’accusé devant cette juridiction. Dès l’ouverture de l’audience, le collectif des avocats de l’ancien magistrat et ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême a soulevé une question relative à la composition de la formation de jugement. Selon la défense, certains magistrats appelés à juger Algassimou Diallo avaient également pris part à la décision autorisant les poursuites contre lui. « Au niveau de la décision prise par le bureau de la Cour suprême, les membres de ce bureau, il y en avait qui étaient membres de la formation en charge de juger monsieur Algassimou Diallo. Nous avons donc estimé que des magistrats qui ont pris part à une décision ayant conduit à l’autorisation de la poursuite de monsieur Algassimou Diallo ne pouvaient pas se retrouver dans la formation qui devait également le juger ». À la suite de cette observation, les avocats de l’accusé ont introduit une demande formelle de récusation visant trois magistrats, dont Ibrahima Sory I Tounkara, Yaya Boiro et Fatou Bongoura. Selon l’avocat, cette demande était formulée « contre les magistrats qui ont pris part à la délibération du bureau de la Cour suprême pour autoriser sa poursuite ». Saisie de cette requête, la Cour suprême s’est retirée pour délibérer. Après plus de trois heures de suspension, elle a repris l’audience et notifié « un arrêt rejetant la récusation de ces différents membres du bureau qui sont également membres de la formation en charge de juger monsieur Algassimou Diallo ». À la suite du rejet de la demande de récusation, le collectif d’avocats a immédiatement introduit une requête en annulation de l’ordonnance renvoyant Algassimou Diallo devant les chambres réunies pour y être jugé des faits qui lui sont reprochés. Au cours des débats, les conseils de l’accusé ont invoqué plusieurs dispositions du Code de procédure pénale, estimant que les droits fondamentaux de leur client n’avaient pas été respectés au cours de l’instruction. « Sur la violation de ses droits substantiels essentiels de défense, notamment l’article 282 du Code de procédure pénale, qui veut que lorsque le juge d’instruction estime qu’il a fini son instruction, avant de prendre l’ordonnance de règlement, mette le dossier de la procédure par l’organe de son greffier à la disposition des avocats de l’inculpé pour une période de trois jours. À l’effet pour ceux-ci, bien entendu, de présenter ou non des observations qui pourraient aller dans le sens d’un non-lieu possible pour la personne inculpée. Sauf que dans le cas de la présente procédure, cette formalité n’a pas été observée, en ce sens que l’instruction d’une affaire qu’on dit être criminelle s’est tenue en deux jours, lundi et mardi. Mercredi matin, qui était je crois le 3 septembre 2026, nous avons été surpris qu’on nous notifie une ordonnance le renvoyant devant les chambres réunies pour être jugé pour les faits pour lesquels il est donc poursuivi », déplore Me Moussa Diallo. Poursuivant son argumentation, l’avocat a insisté sur l’absence du délai qu’il estime légalement requis pour permettre à la défense de formuler ses observations. « Il n’y a pas un délai de trois jours. Donc, nous avons estimé que la violation de cette formalité-là a porté un coût et une grave atteinte aux droits de monsieur Alghassiamou Diallo. Donc, nous avons demandé que l’ordonnance de renvoi soit annulée pour cela en observant les dispositions des articles 396 et 444 du Code de procédure pénale ». La requête en annulation a donné lieu à des échanges particulièrement vifs entre le procureur général près la Cour suprême, Sidy Souleymane N’Diaye, et les avocats de la défense. À l’issue des débats, la Cour s’est de nouveau retirée pour délibérer. À son retour, elle a rendu sa décision en ces termes : « La Cour reçoit la requête » et, au fond, « elle rejette la demande d’annulation parce que mal fondée ». La défense suspend sa participation au procès À la suite de ces décisions, les avocats d’Algassimou Diallo ont exprimé leur désaccord avec la conduite de la procédure. Estimant que leurs requêtes, qu’ils considèrent fondées, ont été systématiquement rejetées, ils ont annoncé leur décision de suspendre leur participation aux audiences. Le collectif a notamment fait part de ses réserves quant aux conditions dans lesquelles la Cour a statué sur la demande de récusation, soulignant la mention de la présence du ministère public lors de la délibération. « On n’a plus de raison à figurer dans une procédure comme ça. Puisque ce n’est pas un procès qu’on veut juste et équitable, nous n’allons pas appartenir à un procès juste pour, disons, faire le figurant dans une procédure. Et ce que nous avons relevé à travers la première décision qui a quand même intrigué plus d’un, c’est que l’arrêt qui a rejeté la demande de récusation porte la mention que la délibération est faite en présence du ministère public, qui se trouve être notre adversaire dans cette procédure. Alors, je me demande est-ce que, dans ces conditions-là, on peut espérer un procès équitable ? À notre entendant, non. Voilà pourquoi le collectif a décidé de suspendre sa participation à ce procès », a conclu Me Moussa Diallo. Pour rappel, dans cette procédure, l’ancien magistrat Algassimou Diallo est assisté par neuf avocats : maîtres Murielle Houindo, Houleymatou Bah, Lancei 3 Doumbouya, Mama Aissata Fofana, Mamady Soufiane Kouyaté, Alpha Amadou DS Bah, Almamy Samory Traoré, Moussa Diallo et Raffi Raja. L’audience a été renvoyée au vendredi 16 octobre 2026. Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Procès d’Algassimou Diallo : la Cour suprême rejette les requêtes de la défense, qui suspend sa participation est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Kéran : Des acteurs locaux sensibilisés sur le foncier
items.description: Kantè, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Le Comité régional de concertation Etat-secteur privé (CR-CESP) de la Kara a organisé, le jeudi 15 octobre à Kantè, un atelier de sensibilisation et d’échange sur le foncier. La cérémonie a été présidée par le préfet Douti N’Sarma Mabiba en présence de son collègue de Doufelgou, colonel Aziaba Ayi Sessi et du vice-président de la cour d’appel de Kara, Aboudou-Salami Moutaka. Placée sous le thème « Faciliter l’accès à la terre pour les investisseurs et les producteurs locaux », cette activité s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du programme d’activités de l’année 2026 du CR-CESP-Kara. L’objectif est d’éclairer les autorités traditionnelles, les chefs des services déconcentrés, les producteurs et investisseurs ainsi que la population sur les procédures et règlementation d’accès au foncier en vigueur. Il s’agit également d’identifier les contraintes relatives à l’accès à la terre en mettant en exergue les rôles et responsabilités des parties prenantes notamment les autorités coutumières et les services techniques de l’Etat dans la sécurisation foncière. Les travaux ont été marqués par une communication sur le cadre juridique régissant le foncier et des échanges sur le partage d’expériences en matière de contentieux foncier. Le préfet Douti a invité ses administrés à s’approprier les procédures d’accès et de sécurisation foncière afin que les incompréhensions soient réduites pour favoriser des relations plus transparentes entre les différents acteurs. Il a souligné que « le développement des collectivités territoriales dépend de la capacité individuelle et collective de chaque citoyen à créer un environnement favorable à l’investissement et à la production tout en respectant les droits et les intérêts de chacun ». ATOP/PAP/BA
